# Kiwi API

> Kiwi is an HTTP API platform. This file is a self-contained reference written for
> LLM coding assistants - paste it in as context when generating Kiwi client code.
> The authoritative machine spec is at https://api.aallyn.net/openapi.json
>
> STATUS: 1.0 platform (accounts, API tokens, rate limiting, usage metrics) with
> the first data endpoints live: Trove game data under `/v1/rotations/*`. More product
> endpoints are added on top over time - `GET /openapi.json` is always current.
>
> IMPORTANT: Programs authenticate ONLY with an API token. Account sign-up,
> sign-in, and token creation are done by a human in the browser developer portal
> (https://dev.aallyn.net). There is NO programmatic login endpoint - never call
> `/auth/*` from code, and don't generate sign-in/sign-up requests. The API token
> is the only credential a program uses.

## Base URLs

- `https://api.aallyn.net` - the data API (`/v1/*` once published, `/health`). This is what your code calls.
- `https://dev.aallyn.net` - the developer portal (a website). Humans use it to sign up and manage tokens; programs do not call it.

## Authentication

1. A human creates an account and an **API token** in the portal (browser).
2. The token (`kiwi_<43 base62>_<checksum>`, regex `kiwi_[A-Za-z0-9]{43}_[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}`)
   is shown once at creation; store it securely.
3. Programs send it as a bearer credential on every request:
   `Authorization: Bearer kiwi_...`

Tokens are scoped and IP-restricted, and may expire. Enforcement per request:
- IP not on the token's allowlist → `403 ip_not_allowed`
- token missing a required scope → `403 insufficient_scope`
- revoked/expired token → `401 not_authenticated`

There is no refresh, no session, no login round-trip - the token is the credential.

## Conventions

- All request/response bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).
- **Errors** always use this envelope (branch on `code`, not `message`):
  ```json
  { "error": { "code": "rate_limited", "message": "…", "details": { } } }
  ```
- **Rate limits**: responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`,
  `X-RateLimit-Reset` (unix seconds). A `429` adds `Retry-After` (seconds).
- Default data-API limit: **120 requests / minute / token**.
- **Compression**: send `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. JSON responses over 1 KB come back
  gzipped (`Vary: Accept-Encoding`), which matters most on the bulky ones - a big
  `/v1/updates/{branch}/tree` listing shrinks roughly 10×. Streaming responses
  (`/v1/events/stream`) are never compressed, so SSE stays unbuffered.

## Error codes

| HTTP | code | meaning |
|------|------|---------|
| 400 | `bad_request` | malformed request |
| 401 | `not_authenticated` | missing/invalid/expired/revoked API token |
| 403 | `insufficient_scope` | token lacks the required scope |
| 403 | `ip_not_allowed` | request IP not in the token's allowlist |
| 403 | `forbidden` | authenticated but not allowed |
| 404 | `not_found` | resource missing or not yours |
| 422 | `validation_error` | body validation failed (`details` lists fields) |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | rate limit exceeded (see `Retry-After`) |
| 500 | `internal_error` | unexpected server error |

## Scopes (bitmask)

A token carries a bitmask of scopes named `<resource>:<action>`. `0` = all scopes
(present + future); otherwise OR the bits you need. Currently defined:
- `rotations:read` (bit 1) - server time, bonuses, merchants, biomes - **public** (usable with no token, see below)
- `feeds:read` (bit 2) - news, Twitch streams, YouTube/Bilibili videos, Trovesaurus event calendar - **public**
- `stats:read` (bit 4) - raw stat tables (power rank / magic find / light) and class definitions
- `gems:read` (bit 8) - gem simulator (generate/augment), evaluator, and build optimizer
- `misc:read` (bit 16) - third-party modding-software list, time converter, news archive, the market interest-items list, and the supporters credits list (`/v1/misc/interest-items` and `/v1/misc/supporters` are **public** - no token needed)
- `mods:read` (bit 32) - decompile a `.tmod` file and build a `.tmod` from files
- `updates:read` (bit 64) - browse archived game files: versions, per-version changes, directory tree, single-file download
- `codexes:read` (bit 128) - read parsed game codexes (allies, mounts, dragons, wings, auras, boats, sails, flasks, tomes, mag riders, fishing poles, skins, mementos, styles, recipes, items, fish, badges), their relationships, badge requirements and progression trees - **public**
- `btt:read` (bit 256) - read BetterTroveTools releases (latest version per platform, per channel) - **public**
- `leaderboards:read` (bit 512) - read Trove in-game leaderboards (boards, entries, timestamps, player history)
- `market:read` (bit 1024) - read Trove marketplace listings (active listings, distinct items, interest list, per-item summary)
- `activity:read` (bit 2048) - read Trove player-activity estimates (live active-player count + multi-period trend series) - **public**
- `giveaways:read` (bit 4096) - read public giveaways (ongoing draws, prizes, entry counts) - **public**
- `events:read` (bit 8192) - subscribe to the live SSE event stream (real-time rotation/feed pushes: challenge, chaos, merchants, biomes, status, news, giveaways, activity, and `game_update` when a new build is mirrored) - **public**
- `ocr:read` (bit 16384) - read character stats from a stat-sheet screenshot via self-hosted OCR (token required - CPU-heavy)
- `store:read` (bit 32768) - read the in-game Kiwi Store catalog (categories, products, prices, sales, deals, lootbox odds)
- `mods:write` (bit 65536) - manage Mods Hub mods for creators who connected their account to yours (see **Managing a creator's mods** below). The only write scope; it grants nothing on its own.

## Managing a creator's mods (`mods:write`)

Mods on the Hub belong to **Dashboard** accounts (Discord sign-in on trove.aallyn.net), not to API
accounts - so an API account has to be *invited* before it can touch one. The invite is a **creator
token**: one per Dashboard account, generated under **Mods → API access**, and shown once.

1. The creator generates their creator token (`kiwi_creator_…`) and gives it to you.
2. You paste it once on **dev.aallyn.net → Creators** (`POST /v1/mods/hub/creator-links`,
   session-authenticated). That creates a **connection** - the token is a connect code, not a
   credential, and isn't used again.
3. From then on you call the write API with an ordinary API token carrying `mods:write`.

A connection covers **all of that creator's mods, including ones they create later**, until the
creator narrows it to named mods from their Dashboard. They can also revoke one connection, or
rotate their creator token to cut every connection at once. You may hold connections to many
creators, and a creator may connect many API accounts.

What a connection allows: create mods, commit files, cut releases, publish/unpublish/**delete** them,
edit metadata, tags, images and **visibility** (so hiding a mod is an API call), and read the
creator's own mods back including drafts. What it never allows: deleting a **mod**, minting git
tokens, editing the creator's profile, or changing collaborators - those stay with the creator on the
website.

- `GET /v1/mods/hub/creator-links` → your connections; `DELETE /v1/mods/hub/creator-links/{id}` drops one.
- Write calls are the `/v1/mods/hub/projects/*` family, e.g.
  `POST /v1/mods/hub/projects/{handle}/{slug}/releases` (cut a release),
  `PATCH /v1/mods/hub/projects/{handle}/{slug}` (edit, incl. `visibility` and `is_beta`).
- **Release lifecycle**: `PATCH /v1/mods/hub/releases/{release_id}` with `{"status": "published"}` /
  `{"status": "draft"}` publishes or unpublishes a build (it also takes `title` / `changelog`);
  `DELETE /v1/mods/hub/releases/{release_id}` removes one build for good - the mod, its files and its
  other releases are untouched. Unpublishing is the reversible one; prefer it.
- **Silent releases**: pass `silent: true` when cutting a release (`POST …/releases`, or the `silent`
  form field on `POST …/releases/upload`) to ship a build without announcing it - no `mod_release`
  event on the stream, so no webhook and no DM alert, and the mod's `last_release_at` is left where it
  was, so it doesn't move in the `recent` sort. The build is otherwise a normal published release:
  listed, downloadable, newest-wins for update checks. It stays silent permanently - no later
  visibility change announces it. `PATCH …/releases/{id}` takes `silent` too, so a draft can be flipped
  quiet before it is published.
- **Reading your own work back.** The `/v1/mods/hub/*` and `/v1/mods/*` reads all answer as an
  anonymous visitor, so they can't see a draft mod or an unpublished release. The creator-scoped
  mirrors do: `GET /v1/mods/hub/me/projects` (all mods you manage), and per mod
  `GET /v1/mods/hub/me/projects/{handle}/{slug}` (detail, drafts included),
  `…/releases` (every release, drafts and hidden variants included - this is where a `release_id`
  comes from), `…/commits` and `…/placement`.
- The mod in the URL decides which creator you're acting as. On the routes that name no mod
  (`POST /v1/mods/hub/projects`, `GET /v1/mods/hub/me/projects`) add `?creator=<handle>` or the
  `X-Kiwi-Creator` header - optional when you're connected to exactly one creator.
- `403 insufficient_scope` = the token lacks `mods:write`; `403 forbidden` = no connection covers
  that mod, or the action is website-only.

## Endpoints - Data (base: https://api.aallyn.net, auth: API token)

Grouped by function. Rotations/feeds/stats are GET, read-only (timestamps real-UTC **unix seconds**);
the gem/misc tools add POST calculators. Full field schema in `/openapi.json`.

**`/v1/rotations/*`, `/v1/feeds/*`, `/v1/codexes/*`, `/v1/btt/*`, `/v1/activity/*` and `/v1/events/*` are PUBLIC** - callable
with no token at a stricter per-IP rate limit (30 req/min/IP by default). Send a token carrying the matching
scope to get the full per-token limit (120 req/min). Surfaces that fan out - one page of browsing costing many
calls - get widened budgets of their own: **`/v1/codexes/*` gets 5×** (150 req/min/IP anon, 600 req/min/token),
**the `/v1/mods/hub/*` browse reads get 8×** (240 / 960) and **their images + downloads 30×** (900 / 3600) in a
SEPARATE bucket, so a grid of thumbnails cannot starve the browse calls beside it. A malformed/revoked token still 401s; a valid token without the scope is served on
the anonymous per-IP budget. A few individual endpoints are also tokenless (`POST /v1/stats/coefficient`,
`/v1/misc/interest-items`, `/v1/misc/supporters`, `/v1/misc/feedback`, the `/v1/updates` file downloads).
All other surfaces require a token with the matching scope:
`/v1/stats/*` need `stats:read`; `/v1/gems/*` need `gems:read`; `/v1/misc/*` need `misc:read`;
`/v1/mods/*` need `mods:read`; `/v1/updates/*` need `updates:read`; `/v1/leaderboards/*` need `leaderboards:read`;
`/v1/market/*` need `market:read` and `/v1/store/*` need `store:read` (read sides; all three have a `/insert`
endpoint that is **master-only** - it requires a superuser API token).

**Live event stream (SSE).** Push instead of poll: rather than hammering `chaos-chest` /
`challenge/current` at the top of the hour, subscribe once and receive updates the instant a capture lands.
- `GET /v1/events/stream` (scope `events:read`, **public**) → a long-lived `text/event-stream`. On connect
  you get a snapshot of every registered source's current state, then one message per change. Each message
  is an `event: <type>` line + a JSON `data: {type, data, ts}` payload, where `type` ∈ `challenge` | `chaos` |
  `corruxion` | `fluxion` | `longshade` | `wild_mana` | `stampy` | `daily_bonuses` | `activity` |
  `server_status` | `trove_news` | `giveaways` | `game_update` | `mod_release`, and `data` mirrors the matching
  REST body (e.g. `/challenge/current`, `/chaos-chest`; `game_update` carries `{version:{branch,ordinal,version_tag,
  files_added,files_modified,files_removed,...}}` for the latest live-US build). `mod_release` is a **discrete**
  event (not in the on-connect snapshot) fired when a **public** Mods-Hub mod publishes a release, and it carries
  the whole announcement so you never need a follow-up fetch: `data = {project, release, previous, change,
  image_url, download_url, page_url}`, where `project` is the full public mod card (`slug`, `handle`, `title`,
  `summary`, `tags`, `categories`, `author`, `banner_url`, `preview_urls`, `download_count`, `star_count`,
  `page_url`, `api_url`, fork/lineage fields - the long `description`/`readme_text` and their `*_i18n` maps are left out, fetch
  `api_url` for those), `release` is the build (`id`, `tag`, `branch`, `title`, `changelog`, `format`,
  `filename`, `size`, `sha256`, `mod_version`, `properties` = the `.tmod` header, `image_url`, `download_url`,
  `published_at`), `previous` is the same shape for the build it supersedes on that branch (`null` on a first
  release), and `change` summarizes the step (`kind`, `from_tag`, `to_tag`, `size_delta`, `days_since_previous`,
  `release_count`, `artifact_unchanged`). `image_url` is the one image to lead with (the build's preview, else
  the mod banner). Drafts, unlisted and taken-down mods are never announced, and neither are releases on a
  **hidden variant** - if the mod page won't list a build, the firehose doesn't either. **A build fires
  exactly once**, at the first moment the public can see it: publishing a release on a mod that is still a
  draft (or on a hidden variant) announces nothing, and whichever setting was holding it back being lifted -
  the mod **going public**, the **variant being revealed** - announces the current build then. One event
  either way: a mod arriving with a back catalogue is one piece of news rather than one per historic version.
  Nothing re-announces a build afterwards: not unpublishing and republishing it, not flipping the mod to
  draft and back, not re-hiding and re-revealing its variant. A build the creator cut as **silent** is
  never announced at all, at any later moment. Hook it to mirror/announce new mod
  releases. A `: ping` keep-alive comment arrives ~every 20s;
  reconnect on disconnect and the snapshot re-primes you.
  Example: `curl -N https://api.aallyn.net/v1/events/stream`.
  - **Don't want to hold a connection?** The website **User Dashboard** (Discord login at
  trove.aallyn.net) lets a user register a **Discord webhook** that Kiwi POSTs a rendered embed to
  when a `challenge`, `mod_release`, or `game_update` event fires - a push alternative to the SSE
  stream for "post it to my Discord channel". The embed is **fully customizable** (title, color,
  fields, footer, image, message text) with `{variable}` placeholders and a live preview; the same
  editor customizes the Kiwi Discord **bot's** per-server announcements. The embed image can be a
  custom one from the **Image Studio** (Dashboard): a freeform, server-rendered image designer
  (background + text/shape/image layers) whose text can carry the same `{variables}`. Standalone, a
  design renders at a public URL (`GET /site/images/{id}.png`); as an embed image you pick the design
  from a dropdown and the bot/webhook **renders + uploads it fresh per post** (a Discord attachment,
  not a URL - so live data in the image never goes stale behind Discord's image cache). It's a
  Dashboard feature (no API-token surface), so it's not in this reference.

- `GET /v1/rotations/server-time` → `{ now_unix, now_iso, trove_day, daily_reset_at, weekly_reset_at }`
- `GET /v1/rotations/daily-buffs` → `{ current: Buff, week: [Buff x7] }` where Buff =
  `{ name, color, weekday, emoji, normal_buffs[], premium_buffs[], icon, banner }`
- `GET /v1/rotations/weekly-buffs` → `{ current: Buff, rotation: [Buff x4] }` where Buff =
  `{ name, color, weekday, emoji, buffs[], banner }`
- `GET /v1/rotations/corruxion` → `{ active, starts_at, ends_at, seconds_remaining, schedule: [{starts_at, ends_at}] }`
- `GET /v1/rotations/fluxion` → like corruxion plus `state` (`voting`|`selling`|`away`); each schedule item has `state`
- `GET /v1/rotations/gardening` → `{ two_day: W, three_day: W, upcoming: [W] }`, W = `{ name, active, starts_at, ends_at }`
- `GET /v1/rotations/chaos-chest` → `{ active, starts_at, ends_at, seconds_remaining, item: { name, identifier, blueprint, image_url } | null, fetched_at }` - weekly featured item. Source preference: the bot-captured item for the current week (read from the in-game cfg) wins; falls back to the Trovesaurus relay when the bot hasn't reported the current week yet. `blueprint` is resolved from the codex when the source didn't carry one, and `image_url` is a ready-made 256px PNG of it (the tokenless `/v1/codexes/render`, so no extra scope) - hit that endpoint yourself with `blueprint` for any other size. Both are `null` when the name can't be pinned to a blueprint unambiguously (no icon beats a wrong one).
- `GET /v1/rotations/chaos-chest/history?limit=50&offset=0` → `{ items: [{ week_anchor, week_ends_at, name, captured_at }], count, total }` - past chaos-chest captures, newest week first.
- `POST /v1/rotations/chaos-chest/insert` body `{ name }` - **master only** (superuser API token). Server infers the week anchor (Tue 11:00 UTC) from now; idempotent on the (week) level. Subject to the **ingest cooldown** (per-token, per-endpoint; default 1 per 300s; API-token only - session-JWT replays bypass).
- `GET /v1/rotations/challenge/current` → `{ starts_at, ends_at, active, is_friday_window, seconds_remaining, name | null, type | null, captured_at | null }` - the hourly challenge active right now. Cadence: one per hour on most days; on trove Fridays (real-UTC Fri 11:00 → Sat 11:00) it's two per hour (:00 and :30). Each window lasts 20 minutes; `active=false` during the gap that follows. `name` is null when the bot hasn't reported this window yet. `type` is server-derived from `name` using literal case-sensitive matches: `"collection"` (name == `"Collection Challenge"`), `"rampage"` (name == `"RAMPAGE ALERT!"`), `"racing"` (name == `"Racing Challenge"`), `"target"` (name == `"Target Challenge"`), or `"dungeon"` (anything else - every other captured string is a biome-themed Dungeon Challenge).
- `GET /v1/rotations/challenge/history?limit=50&offset=0` → `{ items: [{ window_anchor, window_ends_at, name, type, is_friday_window, captured_at }], count, total }` - past challenge captures, newest window first. Same `type` classification as `/challenge/current`.
- `POST /v1/rotations/challenge/insert` body `{ name }` - **master only**. Server infers the 20-min window anchor from now; `"none"` / empty name returns 400 (the bot is expected to skip those client-side). Subject to the **ingest cooldown** (per-token, per-endpoint; default 1 per 300s; API-token only - session-JWT replays bypass).
- `GET /v1/rotations/calendar` → `{ starts_at, ends_at, generated_at, count, events: [E] }`, E = `{ type, name, starts_at, ends_at, color?, state?, biomes?:[{name,icon}] }` - every recurring rotation (weekly_buff / corruxion / fluxion / gardening_2 / gardening_3 / stampy / mana) flattened across ±365 days, sorted by start. Invasion excluded.
- `GET /v1/rotations/delves[?week=]` → `{ week, is_current, total, count, fetched_at, depths: [floor] }` - a week's delve rotation, floor records relayed from a community delve source (passed through; rich `{ id, depth, biome, zone, boss, enemies, objective, … }`). Defaults to the current week. **Gated behind the `feature_delves_enabled` master toggle (default OFF) - 404s when the feature is disabled.**
- `GET /v1/rotations/delves/weeks` → `{ current_week, items: [{ week, total, count, fetched_at }], count }` - available weeks (metadata only), newest first. Same `feature_delves_enabled` gate as `/delves`.
- `GET /v1/rotations/biomes` → `{ current: R | null, upcoming: [R] }`, R = `{ starts_at, ends_at, biomes: [{name, final_name, icon}] }` (3-hour d15 rotation, 3 biomes)
- `GET /v1/rotations/wild-mana` → same shape as /v1/rotations/biomes (weekly, 3 biomes)
- `GET /v1/rotations/stampy` → same shape (weekly, 48h window, 1 biome)
- `GET /v1/feeds/news?limit=20` (1–50) → `{ items: [{ title, url, author, summary, category, categories[], image, published_at }], count }` - latest only (small live view). Full archive: `/v1/misc/news-history`.
- `GET /v1/feeds/twitch` → `{ items: [{ channel, login, url, title, viewers, game, started_at, thumbnail }], count, fetched_at }` (live streams)
- `GET /v1/feeds/youtube` → `{ items: [{ title, url, channel, video_id, published_at, thumbnail_url }], count, fetched_at }`
- `GET /v1/feeds/bilibili` → same shape as youtube
- `GET /v1/feeds/events[?category=&limit=]` → `{ items: [Event], count }` - events happening **now**. Event =
  `{ event_id, name, url, category, image, icon, lookup, starts_at, ends_at, status, seconds_until }` (unix seconds, real UTC)
- `GET /v1/feeds/events/categories` → `{ categories: [string], count }` - distinct categories (dynamic; new ones appear as events arrive)
- `GET /v1/feeds/events/upcoming[?category=&limit=]` → events not yet started (soonest first); `status="upcoming"`
- `GET /v1/feeds/events/history[?category=&limit=]` → events already ended (most recently ended first); `status="ended"`
- `GET /v1/stats/power-rank` → `{ stat, label, sources: [Source], count }`, Source = `{ name, value, type, percentage, step, permanent }`
- `GET /v1/stats/magic-find` → same shape (Magic Find sources)
- `GET /v1/stats/light` → same shape (Light sources; `step`/`permanent` populated)
- `GET /v1/stats/classes` → `{ items: [Class], count }` - all 18 classes, each carrying its `tech_name`
- `GET /v1/stats/classes/{tech_name}` → one Class by token, e.g. `knight`, `adventurer` (404 `not_found` if unknown). Class =
  `{ tech_name, name, shorts[], damage_type, weapons[], attributes[], stats: [{name,value,percentage,absolute}], bonuses: […], subclass: {name, description, level: {"1":[…]…}, power: {…}}, abilities: [{name,icon,type,stages:[{name,base,multiplier}]}] }`. A subclass grants a stat bonus keyed by its LEVEL (`level`: `"1"`/`"10"`/`"15"`/`"20"`/`"25"`/`"30"`) and a passive whose strength is keyed by the subclass's POWER RANK (`power`: `"1"`/`"5000"`…`"40000"`, the floor of each band) - two different scales, not one. `absolute` marks a value that names the resulting stat rather than a delta (only Fae Trickster's Flying Speed), so it must not be rendered with a `+`; Revenant's Incoming Damage is negative for the same reason.
- `POST /v1/stats/coefficient` (**tokenless**) `{ physical_damage?, magic_damage?, critical_damage }` → `{ coefficient, damage_used: "physical"|"magic", formula }`. Stateless calculator for the in-game character **Coefficient** = `floor(max(physical_damage, magic_damage) * (1 + critical_damage/100))` (`critical_damage` is a percent, e.g. `3438.3`); the higher of the two damage stats is used. Provide `critical_damage` + at least one damage stat (else **400**). Same formula `POST /v1/ocr/character` derives Coefficient with.

For merchants, `seconds_remaining` counts down to leaving (when `active`) or arriving (when not).
News is relayed from `trovegame.com`; Twitch/YouTube/Bilibili are fetched at source (Twitch Helix, YouTube Data API, Bilibili scrape) - all cached server-side in `FeedCache`. Events are stored
(kept after they leave the upstream feed) so history/upcoming work; `status` is `upcoming`|`ongoing`|`ended`
and `seconds_until` counts down to start (upcoming) or end (ongoing).
Stats are raw game data (no calculation): stat tables list each source and how much it gives;
`tech_name` is the stable token to reference a class by (display `name` differs, e.g. `adventurer`→"Boomeranger").

### Gems (`gems:read`) - stateless; gem objects round-trip through the client

A gem is a JSON object `{id, tier, type, element, restriction?, ability?, level, stats:[…], augmentation?,
+ computed: gem_name, quality, power_rank, stat_values, …}`. A stat is `{type, locked, containers:[{base,
augments:[{type,count}]}]}`. Nothing is stored server-side - you hold the gem and POST it back to mutate it.
Use `GET /v1/gems/lookups` for all valid ids (tiers 1-4, types 1 Lesser/2 Empowered, elements 1-4, stat
types 1-9, augments 1 Rough/2 Precise/3 Superior).

- `POST /v1/gems/generate` body `{tier?, type?, element?, restriction?, level?, augmentation?}` (omit→random) → a gem object
- `POST /v1/gems/augment` body `{gem, stat_position (0-2), augment_type (1-3)}` → `{applied, gem}` (applied=false if the stat is already maxed)
- `POST /v1/gems/spark` · `flare` body `{gem, stat_position}` → `{applied, gem}` (reroll stat type / move a proc)
- `POST /v1/gems/level-up` body `{gem}` · `set-level` body `{gem, level}` → `{applied, gem}`
- `POST /v1/gems/evaluate` body `{tier, type, level, stats:[{type,value,extra_containers}]×3, auto_guess_procs?}` → `{quality_percent, calculated_power_rank, stats[], focus_totals, headline_cost, …}`. A gem normally gains a boost at levels 5/10/15, but that is a cap, not a rule - gems short a boost exist, so `guessed_distribution` may total less than `available_extra_containers`, and a hand-entered spread below the cap is kept as given (only a total above it is rejected/re-guessed)
- `POST /v1/gems/evaluate-simple` body `{tier, type, power_rank, level}` → `{quality_percent, min_power_rank, max_power_rank, is_within_range, containers, boosts, focus_totals, headline_cost, …}` (estimate quality from Power Rank alone - no per-stat input). The band is read against the largest container count that actually contains the entered PR, so a gem short a boost reads its own band instead of scoring 0%
- `GET /v1/gems/stat-range?tier&type&stat_type&level&extra_containers[&element]` → `{min_value, max_value, thresholds, …}`
- `GET /v1/gems/builds/options` → valid build-config values (classes, allies, foods, flags)
- `POST /v1/gems/builds/calculate` body BuildConfig `{build_type, character, subclass, food, ally, ally_buff, critical_damage_count, no_face, light, subclass_active, litany, berserker_battler, bounty_hunt, star_chart?, high_precision}` → `{results:[{rank, layout, coefficient, …}], count}` (top 200 by damage coefficient). `high_precision` (default false) rounds every result field to 8 decimals instead of 1-2 - layouts often separate below the 2nd. Ally stats are the level-30 values; `ally_buff` (default true) is Blessing of the Lilypad and multiplies the ally's own Light by 1.155 and its Physical/Magic/Critical Damage by 1.31 - nothing else in the build is touched. Each result carries `crit_bonus` - the percentage that MULTIPLIES the summed critical damage (allies whose crit damage scales the stat rather than adding points to it, plus the star chart's crit percentage); `0` when nothing multiplies it. `bounty_hunt` is the Sundered Uplands boss buff and is ignored unless `star_chart` unlocks it - the "Bounty Hunt Boon" node grants +10% Physical/Magic Damage and the "Bounty Hunt" node upgrades that same buff to +15% (they never stack); read `bounty_hunt.available` off the star-chart parse before offering it.

### Misc (`misc:read`)

- `GET /v1/misc/news-history?limit=50&offset=0` (limit 1–200) → `{ items: [NewsItem], count, total }` - the full news archive (never pruned), newest first, paginated. Same item shape as `/v1/feeds/news`.
- `GET /v1/misc/software` → `{categories:[{key, description, software:[{name, free, url, description}]}], count}` (Trove modding tools). **Public** (tokenless; a `misc:read` token earns the wider per-token rate budget).
- `GET /v1/misc/timezones` → `{items:[{id, name}], count}` - supported zones (`trove`, `UTC`, IANA ids). **Public** (tokenless; a `misc:read` token earns the wider rate budget).
- `GET /v1/misc/time/now` → `{unix, zones:[{id, name, datetime, date, time}]}` - current time in every zone (Trove "server" time = UTC−11). **Public** (tokenless; a `misc:read` token earns the wider rate budget).
- `GET /v1/misc/interest-items` → `{items:[<name>], count}` - sorted allow-list of item names the market scraper bot tracks. **Public** (tokenless OK; a token carrying `misc:read` still earns the wider per-token rate budget). DB-backed; managed via `/admin/market/interest-items` (superuser session, master panel). Seeded from `gamedata/market_items.json` on first boot. Admins can also group items into ordered sidebar **categories** for the `/market` page (`/admin/market/categories` - create/rename/reorder/delete + assign item names); membership is stored by item *name* on the category doc, decoupled from the allow-list, so single deletes and the bulk replace never uncategorize anything. The public `/site/market/items` proxy ships `categories:[{name, items}]` and `untracked:[<name>]` alongside `items`, and the `/market` sidebar renders them as collapsible groups (uncategorized names fall under "Other"; `untracked` = names with stored listings that are no longer on the allow-list - shown under a system "Untracked" group with a no-longer-updating warning, overriding their category until re-added).
- `GET /v1/misc/supporters` → `{supporters:[<name>], count}` - the project's supporters credits list, in display (insertion) order. **Public** (tokenless OK; a token carrying `misc:read` still earns the wider per-token rate budget). Same list shown on the `/support` page; admin-managed via `/admin/supporters` (superuser session, master panel). Seeded with the initial credits on first boot. Cached 5 min.
- `GET /v1/misc/trove-status` → `{ overall, auth:{online,http_status,latency_ms,error}, environments:{ eu:{status,online,game:{online,host,port,latency_ms,error}}, us:{...}, pts:{...} }, checked_at }` - **Public, tokenless.** Live Trove server status from a background prober that runs every ~60s (served from cache, never blocks). `overall` rolls up the public Live regions EU+US ∈ `online`/`maintenance`/`down`/`unknown` (all online → online; all down → down; mixed/partial → maintenance). **auth**: HTTPS liveness of `auth.trionworlds.com` (the shared account-auth gateway) - structured response (<500) + valid TLS = reachable; timeout/refused/TLS-error/5xx = down. Catches full outages but stays UP during world-only maintenance (Akamai). **environments.{eu,us,pts}.game**: a probe of the per-env glsserver port (6560 - the stable login-to-game entry; world-instance ports like :3701x are ephemeral). A bare TCP connect is insufficient: a region in MAINTENANCE still completes the TCP handshake and answers the glsserver hello, then drops the connection (verified in EU's maintenance capture - every attempt got SYN/ACK, a fixed hello reply, empty frames, then FIN, and the client kept retrying), so connect-only reads a false `online`. The **deep probe** (default on, `trove_status_game_deep_probe`) replays a captured glsserver client hello (PER-ENV: `trove_status_{eu,us,pts}_hello_hex`) and counts the region online only if the server HOLDS the socket open for `trove_status_game_hold_seconds` (~1.5s); a server that closes right after a near-empty reply is `maintenance` (measured: EU FINs ~70ms when down vs US/PTS holding 6-28s when up). EU/US are game glsservers that hold a hello-only probe open, so the deep probe works there. **PTS uses an EMPTY hello → connect-only**, because its endpoint (`auth-pcpts01`) is an AUTH gateway that drops a hello-only probe even when up (it would false-flag maintenance). Any anomaly (reset, substantial reply, error) falls back to the connect-only verdict (never worse than before). Per-env verdict: `down` if auth fails; `maintenance` if auth up but the game socket refused/dropped; `online` if auth up + game socket held. **Our-end guard**: a verdict is really "can our box reach Trove", so when a round finds NOTHING reachable (auth AND every region - the signature of our own uplink dropping, not of Trove going dark) the prober first TCP-probes unrelated public anchors (`trove_status_local_check_hosts`, raw IPs of independent operators); if none answer, the round is DISCARDED - no history segment, no snapshot update, no event - and the timeline keeps its last known state. Fails open: any anchor answering (or an empty list) records the outage as normal. Endpoints + deep-probe knobs are runtime-tunable in the admin panel.
- `GET /v1/misc/trove-status/history?env=eu&days=30` (env ∈ eu/us/pts, days 1–90) → `{ env, days, window_start, window_end, uptime, covered_seconds, segments:[{status,online,started_at,ended_at,duration_seconds}], outages:[...] }` - **Public, tokenless.** Status timeline for one environment, persisted as segments (a new segment opens on every status change; the current open one has `ended_at=null`). `outages` is the non-`online` subset; `uptime` is the online fraction over the covered span. Backs the `/status` page downtime-history graphic.
- `POST /v1/misc/time/convert` body `{datetime?: "2026-06-05T14:30", timezone: "trove"|"UTC"|IANA, unix?: int}` →
  `{unix, iso_utc, zones:[{id, name, datetime, date, time}], discord:[{style, label, code:"<t:unix:f>"}]}`.
  Give a naive `datetime` interpreted in `timezone`, or an absolute `unix` (timezone ignored). Discord codes
  render in each viewer's own local time. **Public** (tokenless; a `misc:read` token earns the wider rate budget).
- `POST /v1/misc/feedback` - **multipart/form-data** with fields `message` (5..2000 chars, required), `contact?` (≤200 chars), `category?` (`"bug"|"feature"|"general"`, default `"general"`), `app_version?` (≤64 chars, useful for desktop/3rd-party clients), and up to 4 image `attachments` (each ≤5 MB, MIME `image/png|jpeg|webp|gif`). Returns `{ok: true, received_at}`. **Public, tokenless**, rate-limited per-IP + globally (runtime-tunable, defaults 3 / hour / IP and 60 / hour globally). 429 with `Retry-After` + `X-RateLimit-*` headers on per-IP excess; global cap fails silently. The submitter IP is never persisted; only the message, contact, category, app_version, parsed OS + client (from User-Agent), and the attachment metadata (filename/type/size - bytes go to Discord, not Mongo). On success the entry + attachments are POSTed to the Discord webhook in `feedback.discord_webhook` (runtime config) as a fire-and-forget background task - webhook failures don't fail the submission.

### Mods (`mods:read`) - .tmod decompile + build (stateless; up to 20 MB body)

- `POST /v1/mods/read` - body is the **raw .tmod bytes** (`application/octet-stream`), query `?metadata_only=true|false`.
  Returns `{version, header_size, properties:{modLoader, title, author, flags?, …}, file_count, files:[{path,
  index, offset, size, checksum, content_base64?}], metadata_only, flags, categories[]}`. `metadata_only` omits
  `content_base64`. `checksum` is Trove's FNV-1a-variant (32-bit). Files/paths are lowercase posix. `flags` is the
  category bitmask decoded into `categories` (labels) for convenience (see `/v1/mods/categories`).
- `POST /v1/mods/build` - JSON `{version?: 1, properties: {title, author, modVersion, notes, tags, …},
  files: [{path, content_base64}]}` → **raw .tmod bytes** (`application/octet-stream`, `Content-Disposition`
  attachment). Built in memory and discarded after sending. The `modLoader` header is always stamped `KiwiAPI`
  (any client-sent value is overridden). If `properties.tags` contains category names and no `flags` is set, a
  `flags` bitmask is auto-stamped from them.

### Mods catalog (`mods:read`, tokenless) - browse the shared Mods Hub

App-facing read API for the Mods Hub (below). A mod is addressed by **`<handle>/<slug>`** (handle = the owner's
username; slugs are unique per owner, not globally). Returns **absolute** image / download / page URLs. A *mod*
object carries `{slug, handle, title, summary, description, readme_text, warnings, tags, categories[], flags, author,
is_beta, is_stray, uploaded_on_behalf, banner_url, preview_urls[], download_count, downloads_7d, star_count, popularity_score,
discord_url, website_url, donation_urls[], page_url, created_at, updated_at, forked_from, inspired_by, fork_count}`
(`banner_url` / `preview_urls[]` are the creator's upload at full resolution - up to 5 MB. Append **`?w=400`,
`?w=708` or `?w=1416`** for a WebP downscaled to that width, rendered once and cached forever; any other width
is a 400, and an image already narrower than the one you asked for comes back untouched.)
plus a **`<field>_i18n`** map beside each prose field (`title_i18n`, `summary_i18n`, `description_i18n`,
`readme_i18n` for `readme_text`, `warnings_i18n`): the creator's OWN translations, `{lang: text}` over the site's
language codes (`fr`, `de`, `pt-PT`, `es`, `ru`, `ja`, `ko`, `zh-CN`, `th`). Show the reader's language when it's there,
else the base field - which is always the English one and always present, so a partially translated mod still reads.
`title_i18n` is display only: the slug, the `.tmod`'s internal title and every release filename stay on the base
title. Files-mode mods keep their README translations in the repo instead: `README.md` plus `README.<lang>.md`
beside it. (`readme_text` is the releases-only long-form README; `warnings` is `<br>`-split warning text;
**`is_beta`** is the creator's own "still in
development" flag - a label for players (badge + note on the page), nothing else: a beta mod is public,
listed and downloadable like any other;
**`is_stray`** marks an
unclaimed "stray" mod - uploaded via contributions and not yet tied to a user account - addressed at `stray/<slug>`
and claimable by its author; **`uploaded_on_behalf`** marks an *uploaded* mod - a user shared a mod someone else made:
the uploader owns it (shown as "Uploaded by …") while `author` credits the named creator ("Created by …"). It is
releases-only and NOT claimable, distinct from an *authored* mod where the uploader is the creator);
detail + lookup also include `releases[]` =
`{tag, branch, title, changelog, format, filename, size, sha256, download_count, download_url, published_at}`
(plus `title_i18n` / `changelog_i18n`, the creator's translations of that build's wording; `filename` for a `.tmod`
is the artifact's internal `title` property + `.tmod` - Trove matches a mod by that title in-game, so the download
keeps that exact name).

- `GET /v1/mods` - list published mods (cards, no releases). Query `q` (case-insensitive substring over title/summary/tags/author), `tag`
  (filter by one tag/category), `author`, `sort` ∈ `recent|popular|downloads|stars|new|title`, `limit` (≤100),
  `offset`. Returns `{items, count, total, limit, offset}`. `recent` orders by `last_release_at` -
  when a mod last PUBLISHED a release, not when its page was last edited, so retitling a mod or
  fixing a typo never pushes it back to the top. Cards carry both `last_release_at` (null until a
  first release) and `updated_at` (any edit). A build the creator cut as **silent** deliberately leaves
  `last_release_at` alone, so a mod can carry a version newer than that timestamp.
- `GET /v1/mods/{handle}/{slug}` - full metadata + published releases for one mod (404 if not public).
- `GET /v1/mods/popular` - the **25 most popular** mods (`limit` ≤25). `popularity_score` is a 0.0-1.0 metric
  derived mainly from the **last 7 days** of downloads (with stars + lifetime downloads as a floor), top mod ≈ 1.0.
- `POST /v1/mods/lookup` - JSON `{hashes: [sha256, …]}` (≤200). Resolves mod + release metadata from artifact
  **content hashes** → `{results: {<hash>: {mod, release}}, unknown: [<hash>, …]}`. Identify installed `.tmod`s.
  A release's `sha256` is exactly what its `download_url` serves, so comparing it against the hash of the file on
  disk is a reliable "installed / outdated" check. A build that was repacked to carry a **config** (below) also
  answers to **every hash it used to have**, so a copy installed before the repack still resolves to this release
  - it reads as installed and raises no phantom update (it just doesn't get the config).
- `GET /v1/mods/categories` - the fixed category vocabulary → `{categories: [{name, bit}]}`. A mod's categories
  are stored as tags AND encoded as a `flags` bitmask (sum of bits) on its `.tmod`; test membership with
  `flags & bit`. The build/read tools auto-encode/decode this (see Mods section above: `flags` + `categories`).

Mod **hashes are unique per creator**: a release whose exact artifact (sha256) is already published by another
creator is rejected (anti-reupload). An **uploaded-on-behalf** mod is held to a stricter, *global* bar: its
artifact must not already exist anywhere on the hub at all (anti-duplicate for shared re-uploads).

### Mods Hub - browse/share/develop mods (website feature; not in this API reference)

A stored, git-like hub for sharing & versioning mods (vs the stateless build/read tools above), at
**trove.aallyn.net/mods**; browse + download are public, developing needs a Discord (site) login. A *project*
has banners/previews, **forking** + **inspired-by attribution**, and one of two **modes**:
- **files** - full versioned workflow (git commits/branches/clone) + *releases*. A release is compiled
  server-side from a commit into a selectable **format** (`.tmod` or `.zip`), or an uploaded prebuilt build.
- **releases** - releases-only: the modder just uploads already-built `.tmod`/`.zip` files (no file history).

A built `.tmod` is a *release artifact*, never a versioned file: committing one is rejected on every write path
(the studio's commit form, `POST /projects/{handle}/{slug}/commits`, and `git push`, which reports the ref as
`remote rejected`). It has to go through the release upload instead.

A user can also **upload a mod on someone else's behalf** ("This mod was made by someone else" in the create
form): the uploader owns/manages it but names the real creator, shown as "Uploaded by <uploader> · Created by
<creator>" with an **Uploaded** badge. These are forced releases-only, auto-public, NOT claimable, and their
uploaded builds must be globally unique (the same artifact can't already exist anywhere on the hub). They're
kept deliberately **bare** - since the uploader isn't the author, an uploaded mod carries **no owner links
(Discord/website), no donation buttons, and no inspiration credit**, and can't be forked or credited as
inspiration by others.

**Build contents.** Every release has a **Contents** view: the artifact decoded in place - the `.tmod` header
(format version, every property, the decoded categories) and every packed file as a folder tree with sizes, the
preview image and declared config marked. Any file can be pulled out of it on its own. It's a header-only read,
so nothing is decompressed to show it; a `.zip` release lists its entries the same way.

**Reading a mod's code.** An interface mod is a Flash movie, and everything it does is compiled bytecode inside
it - so listing the `.swf` says nothing about what the mod actually does. Every `.swf` in the Contents view has a
**Code** button that decompiles it back to ActionScript (JPEXS FFDec, server-side) and opens it in a reader: the
movie's packages down one side, one class at a time beside them, with a search that covers the whole movie rather
than the open file. Any class can be copied or saved as its own `.as`. Decompiling is cached against the movie's
own content hash, so the same interface shipped across twenty releases is decompiled once and every later open is
instant. This is a **read** of what's already public - the build is downloadable either way; it just means you can
see what a mod does before installing it. A movie carrying no code (pure artwork) says so, and the button is only
offered where a build actually ships a `.swf`.

**Attaching a config.** A Flash-UI mod reads its settings from a `.cfg` the game keeps in `ModCfgs/`, named after
the mod's title. When cutting a release a modder can attach that file and it's packed into the build as
`ui/<title>.cfg` (the mod's own header title) - compiled or uploaded alike; an uploaded `.tmod` is repacked with
everything else preserved, its header version, properties and packed paths included. Offered **only for a build
that ships a `.swf`** - nothing else reads a config - and hidden everywhere else. It's baked in at build time, so
the artifact and its `sha256` are fixed from then on; the pre-repack hash is kept so hash lookup still recognises
the modder's own copy. The build also stamps a **`configPath`** header property naming that packed path, so a mod
that happens to pack several `.cfg` files still says which one IS the config.

An owner can also attach a config to a release that's **already published**, behind a warning that spells out the
trade-off: the build is rewritten in place and gets a new `sha256` (the superseded one is remembered), so anyone
who already installed it is never prompted to re-download and won't get the config - their copy simply keeps
resolving to this release. Delivering a config to existing installs means cutting a **new release**.

When a release's `.tmod` packs a **`.cfg`**, the mod page offers it as its own **Config** download beside the
main one - a config belongs in the game's `ModCfgs` folder, not the mods folder, so it's needed separately. The
file is read out of the `.tmod` on the fly (no second copy is stored) and served under the name the game
expects: the packed path with its casing restored from the artifact's own `title`/`configPath` property, never
a guessed name. A build that packs more than one `.cfg` offers the one its `configPath` declares; with nothing
declared, each is offered by name (guessing which of them matters would be worse than saying so).

A mod can be marked **beta** (`is_beta`) - the creator saying it's still in development. It's a signal
to players only (a Beta badge on the card and page, plus a short note); it changes nothing about how
the mod is listed, served or downloaded, and it's independent of `visibility`.

Files-mode projects can set **source private** (`source_visibility`) - keeps version history + git for the
owner but exposes only the releases publicly (an internal-tool mode; hides the files view + blocks cloning).
**Branches are variants**: each release carries its branch; the UI groups releases per branch (latest of
each surfaced), and the owner can hide chosen variants' releases from the public - a hidden variant is
hidden everywhere, the release event stream included, and revealing it announces its current build. A **source-locked** mod
(private source / releases-only) can't be **forked** - it can only be credited as **inspiration**.

Each mod can also take **issues and requests**: any signed-in site user opens a thread on the mod page, the
creator replies and closes or reopens it, and both sides get a notification in the site navbar. It's the
creator's call per mod (on by default for new mods; mods that predate the feature start off), and the threads
live on the website - there is no public API for them.

The website-internal hub surface (`/v1/mods/hub/*` + the same-origin `/site/mods/*` proxies) is **intentionally
not in this public reference** - it's driven by the website. The documented, app-facing read API is the **Mods
catalog** section above (`/v1/mods`, `/v1/mods/{slug}`, `/v1/mods/popular`, `/v1/mods/lookup`).

**git access.** Each mod is a real git repo: ``git clone https://api.aallyn.net/git/mods/<slug>.git`` (public &
unlisted clone anonymously; drafts need the owner). To push, generate a **git access token** in the User
Dashboard and use it as the git *password* (any username) - a web "Commit files" and a ``git push`` share one
history.

### Modpacks catalog (`mods:read`, tokenless) - curated bundles of hub mods

At **trove.aallyn.net/modpacks**: a *modpack* groups several published hub mods so a player can grab them all at
once. It stores only **references** to mods (no mod content of its own) and rides the same master toggle as the
hub. Browse + download are public; creating one needs a Discord (site) login.
- **No releases, but variants** - named spin-offs (e.g. "Full"/"Lite"), each an ordered list of mod **entries**;
  one is the default. Each entry references a mod + the mod **variant** (branch) to pull from, and a **version
  lock**: off by default (tracks the mod's latest published `.tmod` on that branch) or pinned to a specific
  release tag. The detail lists every variant + each mod it bundles + the version it resolves to.
- **Download** builds the artifact on the fly: a **`.zip`** (each mod's `.tmod` + a `modpack.json` manifest) or a
  **`.tpack`** (the same container format as a `.tmod` - `build_tpack`, same `modLoader` marker - packing each
  mod's `.tmod`; Trove has no native `.tpack`, it's our own `.tmod`-compatible format, told apart by the extension
  + `manifest` header property). Each packed `.tmod` keeps its exact `<internal title>.tmod` filename (case
  preserved) - Trove validates the filename against the mod's header `title`.

App-facing read API (absolute image / page / download URLs, like the Mods catalog):
- `GET /v1/modpacks` - list public modpacks (cards). Query `q` (case-insensitive substring over title/summary/tags), `tag`, `author`,
  `sort` ∈ `recent|downloads|stars|new|title`, `limit` (≤100), `offset`. → `{items, count, total, limit, offset}`.
  A card = `{slug, handle, title, summary, tags, author, banner_url, preview_urls[], download_count, star_count,
  variant_count, mod_count, default_variant, page_url, created_at, updated_at}`.
- `GET /v1/modpacks/{handle}/{slug}` - full detail (404 if not public): the card fields plus `description`,
  `warnings`, `discord_url`, `website_url`, `donation_urls[]`, and `variants[]` =
  `{name, label, mod_count, available_count, download_url, zip_url, mods: [{handle, slug, title, author, variant,
  version, version_locked, available, page_url, author_url}]}` (`version` is the build it resolves to - latest
  unless locked; `available:false` flags a mod with no current build; `author_url` links to the mod author's page).
- `GET /v1/modpacks/{handle}/{slug}/download?variant=&format=tpack|zip` - download a variant (defaults to the
  pack's default variant, `.tpack`). Built on the fly so unlocked mods resolve to their latest build.
- `GET /v1/modpacks/for-mod/{handle}/{slug}` - the **reverse link**: public modpacks that include a given mod
  (by the mod's `<handle>/<slug>`). → `{items: [<card>, …], count}`. Lets a mod page surface the packs bundling it.

The website-internal surface (`/v1/modpacks/hub/*` + same-origin `/site/modpacks/*`) is website-driven and **not
in this reference**; the documented app-facing API is the three endpoints above.

### Embeddable viewers (`mods:read`) - preview tokens for the iframe viewer

Kiwi's 3D model / assembled-creature / `.pkfx` viewers **and its sound player** can be embedded on another
site as an iframe (`trove.aallyn.net/embed/viewer`). Embedding itself needs no token - it's allowed
per-origin by an admin.
**Or drive the viewer directly**, without the iframe, the way a site with its own UI around it does:
one `<script src="https://trove.aallyn.net/static/model_viewer.min.js" defer></script>`, then
`ModelViewer.mount(el, { url, bar, apiBase: 'https://api.aallyn.net' })`. The script loads what else it
needs (three.js, the shared animation bar `anim_clips.js`) from the host it was itself served from, so
one tag stays enough as that list changes, and a piece it cannot load costs that piece rather than the
model. `apiBase` says where `/site/*` answers - omit it and the animation clips, the rig's move graph and
the specular atlas are requested as same-origin paths, which only works if your page proxies them (an
`<img>` is invisible to a `fetch` wrapper, so the atlas is fetched too). The viewer's public assets
(`/site/rigs/*`, `/site/dressing/*`, `/site/render/brdf-map.png`) answer **any** origin, wildcard and
uncredentialed.

Only the upload is an API call, and it exists so a partner can preview a mod **they** host:
- `POST /v1/embed/tmod` - multipart `file=@Mod.tmod` (max 8 MB) → `{token, size, expires_in, reused, viewer_url}`.
  **The file is NOT stored**: it's held in Redis for `expires_in` seconds (default 30 min) and then dropped -
  never written to disk, nothing to purge. The TTL does NOT slide while a visitor watches, so post the mod as
  the partner's page RENDERS rather than caching the token. The token is the file's SHA-256, so re-posting an
  unchanged mod refreshes the same entry instead of holding a second copy.
- `GET /v1/embed/tmod/{token}` (tokenless) → `{token, live, size?}` - check before a visitor hits it.

Everything else about embedding - the iframe URL, sources (`release=` / `tmod=` / `game=` / `prefab=` /
`dress=`), options and the loader script - is a **separate integration guide, not part of this API
reference**: https://docs.aallyn.net/embed

`prefab=<path>` frames a whole game creature - mount, dragon, ally, mob or costume - named the way the game
names it (`prefabs/collections/mount/duck_dragon.binfab`, `prefabs/skins/adventurer_artist.binfab`; the
`.binfab` and the folder are optional when the filename is unambiguous). Rig, animation clips and every part
come from the live game files, so there is nothing to host or upload. Only prefabs the game binds a skeleton
to are addressable, and a bare name more than one creature is filed under (`beetle_firebug` exists four times
over) is refused with a real full path in the message rather than resolved to a guess.

`game=<path>.bnk` frames the **sound player** instead of a 3D stage: a filterable list of every sound in a
Wwise bank with a transport (waveform seek, loop, volume, download) docked above it. `sound=<id or name>`
pins one sound and drops the list, which is the shape a page showing off a single effect wants
(`?game=ui.bnk&sound=ui_gems_upgrade_sm_01`). It reads the same cached bank index the `/updates` sound
browser does, so the manifest decodes nothing and only the sound a visitor plays is decoded. A hub
`release=` whose `.tmod` bundles a `.bnk` plays too; an **uploaded** `tmod=` deliberately does not, because
indexing a bank files every sound into the content store and an upload is held in memory only.

### Updates (`updates:read`) - archived game files (latest version)

Kiwi mirrors Trove's update CDN and stores each version's files content-addressed (deduped). Browse them:
- `GET /v1/updates/branches` → `{ items: [{ branch, current_version, current_ordinal, last_probe_at, status, file_count }], count }` (branches: `live-us`, `pts`)
- `GET /v1/updates/{branch}/versions[?limit=&offset=]` → `{ items: [{ ordinal, version_tag, captured_at, files_added, files_modified, files_removed, bytes_added }], count, total }`
- `GET /v1/updates/{branch}/changes[?version=&ordinal=&type=&limit=&offset=]` → `{ branch, ordinal, version_tag, entries: [{ path, type, content_sha256, size }], count, total, files_added, files_modified, files_removed }` - the per-file diff a version introduced (`type` ∈ `added,modified,removed`). Pin the version by `version` tag or `ordinal`; omit both for the latest. `type` filters to one kind.
- `GET /v1/updates/{branch}/tree[?prefix=]` → `{ branch, prefix, entries: [{ name, path, is_dir, file_count, size, last_ordinal, last_modified_at }], count }` - one directory level (prefix `prefabs/` lists its children); empty prefix = root. `last_ordinal` = the newest version that touched this entry (for a directory, the max over everything beneath it), and `last_modified_at` its `captured_at`; the `/updates` page uses them for the "Last modified" sort. `0`/`null` on files captured before the field existed — the admin **Updates archive → Backfill last-modified** action recomputes them from the change-log.
- `GET /v1/updates/{branch}/file/meta?path=` → `{ path, content_sha256, size, archive, archive_index, removed, removed_ordinal }`. A path the game has since deleted resolves to its **last version before the removal** (`removed:true`, `removed_ordinal` = the version that dropped it) rather than 404ing - a deletion stores no bytes, so the blob comes from the capture before it. 404 only when the path was never archived on that branch. `/file` and `/file/view` follow the same rule, so a removed file still downloads and still previews.
- `GET /v1/updates/{branch}/file?path=` → the raw file bytes (`application/octet-stream`, streamed). **Public, tokenless** (so files can be linked directly); the other updates endpoints still need `updates:read`. Works for loose and TFA-extracted files alike. Because the `/updates` browser paints a whole FOLDER of textures at once (a store dir holds 500+ `.dds`), this endpoint meters in its OWN widened bucket (`updates_file_rate_limit_multiplier`, default 20× = 600 req/min/IP anon) instead of the shared 30/min anon cap - otherwise a texture grid trips the limit and some tiles fail to load. The bytes are an immutable content-addressed blob, so the response is `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400` (+ FileResponse's ETag/Last-Modified for conditional 304s), letting the CDN/browser serve repeat tiles without re-hitting the origin.
- `GET /v1/updates/{branch}/file/view?path=` → `{ branch, path, size, content_sha256, viewable, kind, reason, truncated, text }` - the in-browser preview payload. `kind` tells the client how to render the file: `text` (`viewable:true`, `text` = the UTF-8 content when ≤1 MB and it decodes cleanly with no NUL byte), `image` (browser-native image — png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/ico/apng — rendered via `<img>` straight from the raw `/file` endpoint, no size cap), `dds` (DDS texture — the site decodes it to a `<canvas>` client-side and offers a "download as PNG"), `blueprint` (`.blueprint` voxel model — opens the 3D viewer via the `/site` blueprint endpoint below), `swf` (Flash interface movie — opens the embedded-asset gallery via the `/site` swf endpoints below), `bnk` (Wwise sound bank — opens the sound browser via the `/site` bnk endpoints below), `pkfx` (PopcornFX particle effect — the source text describes emitters and curves and says nothing about what the effect looks like, so the site plays it in the VFX previewer via the `/site` vfx endpoints below; the raw text is still one `/file` fetch away), `binary` (small non-text file ≤1 MB — the client fetches the raw bytes and renders a hex viewer), `too_large` (non-image file above 1 MB) or `missing`. `reason` mirrors `kind` for the non-text cases (kept for older clients). `removed:true` (+ `removed_ordinal`) means the file is gone from the tree and what you get is its last version before the removal.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/file/blueprint?path=` → decoded voxel payload `{ path, count, size:[sx,sy,sz], x,y,z,rgb,kind,level }` (plus `spec`, the per-voxel specular-map index 0-7, when any voxel carries one) for one `.blueprint` in the latest tree, consumed by the web 3D viewer (`blueprint_viewer.js`). Same body shape as the Mods Hub `/releases/{id}/blueprint` endpoint (both reuse `render/voxel.pack_blueprint`). Decoding happens once per file: the payload is cached against the blueprint's own content hash (`render/bp_cache.py`) and served gzipped with an `ETag`, so send `If-None-Match` and a repeat fetch costs a 304. `X-Kiwi-Cache: hit|miss|off` on the response says whether it came from that cache. Add `&fmt=bin` for the compact **KVX1** binary container (same fields, per-voxel arrays as raw little-endian bytes: a JSON header carries `_bin: {path: [offset, count, dtype]}` and the arrays follow, 4-byte aligned, after it) - what the web viewer fetches; `fmt=json` is the default. Site-only helper; 413 (too large) / 422 (empty / undecodable) carry the standard `{error:{code,message}}` envelope, whose `message` the viewer surfaces.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/file/swf?path=` → `{ branch, path, content_sha256, swf: { version, compression, width, height, frame_rate, frame_count }, inventory: { shapes, sprites, fonts, texts, sounds, morphs, buttons, videos, binary, scripts }, assets: [{ id, name, source, codec, width, height, mime, bytes, thumb }], count }` - every **image embedded in a Flash interface movie** (`ui/*.swf`), which is where Trove keeps its UI art. Reads the SWF tag stream (`app/trove/swf/`) and decodes the five bitmap tags - `DefineBits` (6), `DefineBitsLossless` (20), `DefineBitsJPEG2` (21), `DefineBitsJPEG3` (35), `DefineBitsLossless2` (36), `DefineBitsJPEG4` (90) - normalising each to something a browser can show: the lossless tags are raw deflated pixels in four layouts (indexed / RGB555 / premultiplied ARGB) and become PNG, a JPEG whose transparency lives in a separate zlib alpha plane is composited and becomes PNG, and anything already browser-native passes through untouched (`mime` says which). `id` is the SWF character id; `name` is recovered by walking the reference graph backwards from the exported symbols (`SymbolClass`/`ExportAssets` → sprite → shape fill → bitmap), so it is **best-effort** - a bitmap only ever attached from ActionScript has no static reference and comes back `null`. `inventory` counts the non-bitmap tags, so a script-only interface mod is visibly "0 images" rather than an error. Extraction is cached against the movie's own content hash (`render/bp_cache.py`) and the decoded images live in the shared content store, so one decode covers every game version that ships the file unchanged. Site-only helper; 422 when the bytes aren't a readable SWF.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/file/swf/asset?path=&id=[&thumb=1]` → the bytes of one extracted image (`image/png`, or `image/jpeg`/`image/gif` when it passed through untouched). `id` is the character id from the manifest above and is validated against it. `thumb=1` serves the ≤128 px gallery copy when there is one (images already that small have no separate thumbnail and serve the original). Immutable content, so `ETag` + `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`; send `If-None-Match` for a 304.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/file/swf/zip?path=` → every extracted image from one movie as a single `.zip` (`<id>_<symbol>.<ext>`, stored uncompressed - PNG/JPEG are already compressed). 404 when the movie holds no images, 413 above 256 MB.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/file/bnk?path=` → `{ branch, path, content_sha256, bank: { version, bank_id, sections, objects, events }, sounds: [{ id, name, group, path, source, notes, codec, channels, sample_rate, duration, bytes, object_id, error }], count, playable, total_duration }` - every **sound embedded in a Wwise SoundBank** (`audio/*.bnk`), which is where Trove keeps all of its audio. Reads the bank container (`app/trove/audio/`) - `BKHD` (bank version, always 128 for Trove), `DIDX` (the media index), `DATA` (the `.wem` blobs) and `HIRC` (the object graph, read only for which Sound object plays which media). **Names come from the sidecar Wwise writes beside each bank** (`audio/ui.bnk` → `audio/ui.txt`): a bank identifies everything by 32-bit id and carries no strings at all, but that build log maps every media id to its real name and Wwise object path, which is why sounds list as `ui_gems_upgrade_sm_01` rather than `#1099092`. `group` is the second-to-last segment of that object path - the container the sound sits in - so the numbered variations of one effect (`..._01` through `..._04`) fold back together without walking the object graph. The manifest **decodes nothing**: indexing an 87 MB music bank reads only the header, the index and the sidecar, and each `.wem` is filed into the shared content store on the way past. Cached against the bank's *and* the sidecar's content hashes (`render/bp_cache.py`), so a rename-only rebuild still invalidates. `error` is non-null for a media object that cannot be read, which keeps it listed instead of silently missing. Site-only helper; 422 when the bytes aren't a readable bank.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/file/bnk/audio?path=&id=[&raw=1]` → one sound, decoded to something a browser plays natively. Wwise stores three codecs and each needs different work: **Wwise Vorbis** (`0xFFFF`, ~76% of Trove's audio) comes back as `audio/ogg` - the Vorbis packets are *not* re-encoded, only re-wrapped, since Wwise strips the three Vorbis headers, the Ogg framing, each packet's leading type bit and the window flags on long blocks, and replaces the Huffman codebooks with 10-bit indices into a shared library that ships in the Wwise runtime rather than in the file (`app/trove/audio/packed_codebooks_aoTuV_603.bin` supplies it); **Wwise ADPCM** (`0x0002`) is 4-bit IMA in per-channel 0x24-byte blocks and is decoded to `audio/wav`; **PCM** (`0xFFFE`) only needs a new header. `raw=1` serves the game's own undecoded `.wem` instead. Decoding happens per sound and on demand, so playing one effect never touches the other 1,675 in the bank. Immutable content, so `ETag` + `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`; send `If-None-Match` for a 304. 422 when that one sound cannot be decoded.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/file/bnk/zip?path=` → every playable sound from one bank as a single `.zip`, foldered by Wwise container (`<group>/<name>.ogg|.wav`, stored uncompressed). 404 when the bank holds no playable sounds, 413 above 512 MB.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/vfx[?q=&limit=&offset=]` → `{ branch, items: [{ path, size, thumb }], count, total }` - every **PopcornFX particle effect** (`.pkfx`) the branch ships, backing the `/updates` page's **VFX previewer** tab. Trove ships ~9,000 of them, so `q` is a case-insensitive substring of the path and the list is paged rather than handed over whole. Ordered by *filename*, not path - effects are named, not filed, and the handful that sit outside the main folder shouldn't jump the alphabet. `thumb` is the archive path of the still the game's own PopcornFX editor rendered for that effect (`…/Editor/Thumbnails/Particles/<name>.pkfx.png`), or `null`: it is looked up in the tree, never derived, so a listed thumbnail always exists and loads from the tokenless `/v1/updates/{branch}/file` endpoint. One projected scan of the branch's tree builds both this list and the resolver below, cached until the branch takes a new build.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/vfx/manifest?path=` → `{ branch, path, pkfx, deps: [{ ref, basename, source }], missing, game_available }` - one effect's `.pkfx` source plus every asset it references, for the web player (`site/static/pkfx`, the same one the Mods Hub and the embeddable viewer mount). Trove ships a single PopcornFX pack - the folder holding `popcornproject.xml` - and every reference inside an effect is relative to its root, so `Textures/vfx_ray_01.dds` is exactly that path under the pack. The match is **case-insensitive** (the archive stores the CDN manifest's spelling and the effects disagree with it: `VFX_circle_10.dds` ships as `vfx_circle_10.dds`) but still an exact *path* match - a reference the branch doesn't ship comes back `source: "missing"` rather than resolved to a same-named file elsewhere in the game, and the player says "partial preview" instead of quietly drawing the wrong texture.
- `GET /site/updates/{branch}/vfx/asset?path=` → the bytes of one texture/mesh/atlas/child-effect an effect references, resolved by the same rule (`path` is the reference as written in the `.pkfx`, not an archive path). Limited to render-relevant types inside the pack, so it stays a resolver rather than a second file API - the same bytes are already public through `/v1/updates/{branch}/file`. Immutable content, so `ETag` + `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`; send `If-None-Match` for a 304.
- `POST /site/sound-studio/build` (multipart) → the rebuilt bank, as a `.bnk` or wrapped in a `.tmod`. Backs the **Sound Studio** page (`/sound-studio`), where a player silences a sound, swaps one for their own audio, or adds a brand-new one. `spec` is a JSON form field - `{branch, path, codec: "adpcm"|"pcm", output: "bnk"|"tmod", mod: {title, author}, edits: [...]}` - and each `edits[]` entry is `{kind:"mute", id}`, `{kind:"replace", id, clip, channels, rate}` or `{kind:"add", event, clip, channels, rate}`. Replacement audio rides alongside as file parts named `clips`, whose *filename* is the `clip` key, and is **raw interleaved 16-bit PCM**: the browser decodes whatever the user picked (Web Audio already reads mp3/wav/ogg/flac/m4a) and resamples it in an `OfflineAudioContext`, so the server carries no audio decoder and no ffmpeg. **Wwise Vorbis cannot be encoded** - its codebooks live in Audiokinetic's encoder and no open implementation exists - so replacements are written as Wwise ADPCM (default, ~¼ the size) or PCM, both of which Trove's own banks already ship, proving the runtime plays them. A rebuild re-lays DIDX 16-byte aligned, rebuilds DATA, and refreshes each Sound object's own `uInMemoryMediaSize` in HIRC (stale there = the engine reads the wrong byte count). Muting is a replacement with silence rather than a deletion, so nothing referencing the media is left dangling. **Adding** appends the media plus three HIRC objects - a Sound cloned from an existing one (its parameter tree is inherited rather than authored), and a Play Action and Event written from scratch - with the Event id set to the FNV-1 hash of the chosen name, which is what `ExternalInterface.call("POST_SOUND_EVENT", "…")` in a modded Flash UI resolves through. Nothing is stored: the bank is read from the archive, edited in memory, and streamed back. Body cap `sound_studio_max_request_body_bytes` (32 MB); the endpoint also caps per-clip (16 MB) and per-request (28 MB) audio and 200 changes. Site-only helper, gated by `feature_sound_studio_enabled`.

### Codexes (`codexes:read`) - structured game data parsed from the archive

Eighteen typed datasets parsed from `prefabs/*.binfab`, names resolved via the `languages/` locale tables. Stored in Postgres and **relational**: `codex_entry` holds one row per `(branch, path)` (the two branches `live-us`/`pts` are the two "modes"), with the decoded detail lifted into `codex_stat` (one row per numeric bonus), `codex_ability`, `codex_link` (typed relationship edges, indexed BOTH ways), `codex_requirement` (badge rank ladders) and `codex_upgrade` (progression nodes). `codex_entry` also carries a generated `tsvector` for full-text search. Re-indexed after each archive sync (full build once, then only the changed prefabs; `content_sha256` ties each row to its source file). All default to branch `live-us` (`?branch=pts` for PTS). Each entry has identity (name/category/description/tradable) + decoded collectible bonuses: `mastery` (normal, from `meta/multipliers.binfab`), `mastery_geode` (geode-mode, from `meta/geode_multipliers.binfab`), `power_rank`, and a `data` blob of numeric stat bonuses, visible/hidden ability refs, geode-companion upgrade-tree levels, recipe catalogue/providers, and style identity.
- `GET /v1/codexes/types[?branch=]` → `{ branch, items: [{ type, count }], count }` - types present: `ally`, `mount`, `dragon`, `memento`, `style`, `recipe`, `item`, `fish`, `badge`, `wings`, `aura`, `boat`, `sail`, `flask`, `tome`, `magrider`, `fishingpole`, `skin`
- `GET /v1/codexes/search[?branch=&q=&type=&category=&tradable=&stat=&ability=&sort=&limit=&offset=]` → `{ branch, type, query, items: [Entry], count, total }` - cross-type search (all filters optional + ANDed; each `Entry` has its own `type`). `q` = name/description substring; `sort` ∈ `name,-name,category,-category,mastery,-mastery,mastery_geode,-mastery_geode,power_rank,-power_rank,indexed_at,-indexed_at,stat_value,-stat_value`. `stat` (a `$Stat_…` key or bare name) keeps only entries granting it AND adds `stat_value` + `stat_percent` to every row - the best value that entry gives for it, which is what the `stat_value` sorts rank on; without `stat` those sorts fall back to `name`. `ability` (an `abilities/…` ref) keeps only entries referencing it, hidden/mechanical refs excluded
- `GET /v1/codexes/{type}[?branch=&search=&category=&tradable=&stat=&ability=&sort=&limit=&offset=]` → `{ branch, type, items: [Entry], count, total }` - `search` matches name OR description; `category` is exact; `tradable` is a bool; `stat` / `ability` behave exactly as on `/search`
- `GET /v1/codexes/{type}/categories[?branch=]` → `{ branch, type, items: [{ category, count }], count }` - distinct categories for filter dropdowns
- `GET /v1/codexes/{type}/stat-keys[?branch=]` → `{ branch, type, items: [{ stat, stat_name, count }], count }` - every stat entries of that type actually grant, A→Z by display name, `count` being ENTRIES rather than stat rows so it matches what filtering on it returns. The options for `?stat=`
- `GET /v1/codexes/{type}/abilities[?branch=]` → `{ branch, type, items: [{ ref, name, description, count }], count }` - the displayed abilities entries of that type reference, most common first. The options for `?ability=`
- `GET /v1/codexes/{type}/entry?path=[&branch=]` → one `Entry` by its source prefab path
- `GET /v1/codexes/render?blueprint=<logical name>[&branch=&dim=256]` → an `image/png` (not JSON): a game-like voxel render of the blueprint, emulating Trove's `-tool catalog` (perspective camera, flat lighting, glass transparency, transparent background). `dim` 32-512. Cached in Redis and served `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`. 404 when the blueprint isn't on the branch, 422 when it decodes but can't be rendered (an empty placeholder - usually a component part rather than a whole model). Feed it an `Entry.blueprint`. Add `&prefab=<Entry.path>` for a **mount or dragon** and you get the whole creature assembled from every blueprint its rig binds, instead of the one part the row names - no single blueprint is the animal, and the game's own `_ui` icon is a small stand-in (a dragon's is ~600 voxels against ~3,500 assembled). 1,028 of 1,212 mounts + dragons assemble; the rest silently fall back to `blueprint`, as does any creature whose parts can't all be supplied (a half-assembled mount would be worse than a whole part). The site pages use a same-origin twin, `/site/codexes/render`, with the identical status contract - the two causes stay distinguishable there too, since "no image on this card" is otherwise indistinguishable from the browser.
- `GET /v1/codexes/links?path=<Entry.path>[&branch=&direction=out|in&rel=&limit=]` → `{ branch, path, direction, items: [{ rel, path, type, name, category, blueprint, qty, data }], count }` - the typed relationships of one entry, joined to the far end. `rel` ∈ `crafts` (recipe → what it produces), `ingredient` (recipe → what it consumes), `craftable_at` (recipe → a bench/profession, `data` carries `lane` + the in-game crafting tab), `unlocks` (anything → what owning/using it grants), `upgrade_cost` (a progression node → an item it costs), `member_of` (collectible → its catalogue, `data.group` = the group it's filed under). **The reverse direction is the point**: `direction=in&rel=ingredient` on a material answers "what recipes use this", which nothing else can answer - the same rows read from the other end, so it costs no extra decode and no extra table. A link whose far end isn't an indexed prefab is still returned (the edge is real even when the target isn't a codex row); its `type`/`name` are then null/empty.
- `GET /v1/codexes/stats?stat=<$Stat_… or bare name>[&branch=&type=&limit=&offset=]` → `{ branch, stat, items: [{ path, type, name, category, blueprint, stat, stat_name, value, is_percent, slot }], count, total }` - everything that grants a stat, strongest first. One row per entry: a prefab granting the stat in several equip slots contributes its best, so the ranking reflects what an entry actually gives. `slot` is `$EquipmentSlot_Mount|Cart|Wings|Boat` when the bonus only applies in that slot (a boat carries three separate slot blocks), else null. A stat's `…Bonus` key (`$Stat_PhysicalDamageBonus`, "Physical Damage Bonus") is the MULTIPLICATIVE form of it: the game's `MultiplySum` operation scales the stat by the percentage, where a plain `$Stat_PhysicalDamage` record adds a flat amount to it. Both are stated as percentages for some stats - `+30% Critical Damage` is 30 points as an add and 900 as a bonus on a 3,000% sheet - so they rank separately rather than sharing one name.
- `GET /v1/codexes/requirements?collection=<collections/badge/…>[&branch=]` → `{ branch, collection, items: [{ rank, rank_name, collection, badge_id, completion_kind, requirement_key, label, amount, difficulty, status, context }], count }` - what a badge asks for at each rank, bronze first. Every rank of the ladder is returned regardless of which one you ask about (each rank is its own collection path, so asking by collection alone would return exactly one row). `completion_kind` ∈ `metric`, `dragonsouls`, `STBossKilled`, `UpgradeGems`, `SubClassEquipped`, `minprestigelevelsacrossclasses`, `entitlementUnlocked`, `tinyquesttotalpetsoflevel`, `tinyquestconcurrentbuffedpets`, `friends`, `loyalty`, `referafriend`, `none`. `label` is the human-readable requirement ("Blocks Destroyed", "Defeat the Shadow Hydrakken on Ultra difficulty"); `status` is `decoded` or `blocked` - a rank we can't decode is still listed, because the rank exists whether or not its payload reads.
- `GET /v1/codexes/upgrades[?branch=]` → `{ branch, items: [{ system_kind, system_key, nodes }], count }` - the progression systems present. `system_kind` ∈ `geode_module` (Barrier Generator, N-Charge, Omni-Tool, …), `geode_companion` (per rarity), `class_prestige` (the per-class Paragon trees).
- `GET /v1/codexes/upgrades/{system_key}[?branch=]` → `{ branch, system_key, items: [{ system_kind, system_key, node_key, rank, costs, requires, effects }], count }` - one tree's nodes in rank order. `costs` = `[{ item, quantity }]` (the materials that node takes, read from `upgrade/trees/`), `effects` = `{ name, name_key, description, desc_key, abilities: [ref] }` (what it grants, read from the sibling `upgrade/upgrades/`); `requires` names other nodes stated as prerequisites - evidence, not a complete graph, so an empty list means "none stated here", never "no prerequisites". `effects` is `{}` where the node grants no named ability (a plain numeric bump), which stays distinguishable from "the file didn't say".
- `Entry` = `{ type, path, name, category, description, tradable, mastery, mastery_geode, power_rank, blueprint, data, indexed_at }` (`path` is the stable id; `mastery`/`mastery_geode` = collectible mastery, null for non-collectibles; `power_rank` null when absent). `blueprint` is the entry's model, resolved against the branch's real blueprint tree and `null` when nothing matches - a name that renders is worth more than a name that looks right, so unmatched candidates are dropped rather than stored. Two wrinkles worth knowing: a multi-part creature (carpets, bulldozers, warhorses, dragons) lists every component it assembles from, and those parts are empty placeholders, so the whole-model `…_ui` blueprint is preferred over them, and where a creature ships no whole model at all (the warhorse/bull mounts) the largest part it does name is used rather than a blank one; and a **recipe** prefab names no model at all, so it borrows the blueprint of the item it crafts (`data.recipe.output.path`) - `null` when that output has none or can't be read. Placeable products (decorations, blocks) name no model either - theirs comes from the game's own placeable table, which states the model for ~2.8 k of them; the handful that table omits fall back to a naming convention (`placeable/deco/<stem>` -> `deco_<stem>`) gated on matching exactly one blueprint, so an ambiguous name yields `null` rather than a guess. Terrain blocks are textured cubes with no model at all, so most block recipes have no image. `data` carries: `stats` (numeric bonuses: `{ stat: $Stat_…, stat_name (resolved display name), operation, amount, value, is_percent, label, slot, slot_name, component, level }`), `abilities` (`{ ref, hidden, name?, key?, description?
