}` - hidden refs are evidence, not displayed bonuses. `name`/`description` are read from the REFERENCED ability prefab's own locale keys, not constructed from the ref: the description key has more than one shape in the archive, and most ability prefabs carry no name key at all. **`name` is absent when the game names nothing** - it is never the ref prettified into a label, which produced internal ids in title case like "Enemydeath Damagebuff"), for **recipes** `recipe` (`{ output: { path, name, amount }, ingredients: [{ path, name, amount }], requirements: [str], mastery, mastery_source, mastery_prefab_byte?, in_catalogue, catalogue_order?, providers? }` - names resolved by reading the referenced item prefabs; recipe `mastery` is row-local: an exact `meta/multipliers.binfab` row overrides (`mastery_source: "multipliers"`), else the trusted structural byte in the recipe prefab (`"prefab"`, raw value in `mastery_prefab_byte`), else `null` with `mastery_source: "review"` when no trusted/agreeing byte is present. `in_catalogue` = membership in `collection_recipe.binfab` (`catalogue_order` = its source position); `false` marks a source-only recipe. `providers` = the benches/professions a recipe is craftable at (`[{ provider, provider_path, lane }]`, inverted from the crafting-station + profession prefabs that list the recipe - e.g. `placeable/crafting/workbench_chaos_interactive`, `professions/gearcrafting`; lane ∈ bench/profession/vendor/guide/interactive)), for **styles** (hats/faces/weapons/banners, under `style/`) `style` (`{ source_id, equipment_ref (the equipment id it restyles), resolved_id, confidence, family }`; style `mastery`/`mastery_geode` resolve via the equipment id's multipliers row, `null`/review-only when unbacked), and for geode companions `geode_companion` (`{ upgrade_tree, rarity, levels: [{ level, stats, abilities }] }`). The `$…` localization keys (stat/slot names, ability descriptions) are resolved against the archived `languages/` tables at index time.

### Dressing room (`codexes:read`) - compose a Trove character and get its 3D model

Builds a wearable character out of the game's OWN appearance data and assembles it on the same baked class rigs the Mods Hub viewer uses, so one selection renders as a posable, animated model. Everything is read from prefabs, nothing is inferred from filenames: each `prefabs/class/*.binfab` carries a socket table - `(attach bone, equipment slot number)` pairs - which states the class's rig, where a hat/face/weapon attaches, and which weapon families it accepts. That table is the whole compatibility model, and it is the game's: the Knight declares one melee socket, the Candy Barbarian and the Gunslinger declare **two** (which is what "dual wielding" is - one equipped style drawn at both), and the Boomeranger declares a bow socket pair *and* a melee socket, which is why it can carry either. A costume belongs to a class because it binds that class's skeleton; a style fits a socket because its own slot number matches. A style whose family the class has no socket for is reported as dropped, never placed somewhere plausible.

Zero storage: the whole outfit is five stable prefab stems in the query string, so a shared link resolves the same after a game update without any row being written. Tokenless (`codexes:read` earns the higher budget). Toggled by `feature_dressing_room_enabled`; needs the updates archive + rig map indexed. The data plane is a partner API in its own right: `feature_dressing_room_page_enabled` unpublishes only our `/dressing-room` page, leaving `/v1/dressing/*`, `/site/dressing/*` and the embeddable viewer serving, so a site running its own dressing room on this data is unaffected.
- `GET /v1/dressing/classes` → `{ items: [{ key, name, skeleton, weapons: [family], sockets: [{ ap, slot, family }], costumes }] }` - `key` is the class prefab stem (`knight`), `slot` is the game's equipment slot number (24 hat, 26 face, 8 gun, 10 bow, 12 staff, 16 spear, 18 fist, 28 melee), `costumes` is how many are available. Classes with no costume (an ultimate transformation) are not listed.
- **Every slot also takes a raw blueprint**, so a partner with a blueprint name and no style prefab behind it can still render it: pass `equipment_hat_trovesaurus_01[ylva]` (Trove's `[author]` suffix is fine), or a full path like `2026/skins/neonninja_striker/equipment_weapon_sword_neonninja_striker` when the bare name is ambiguous. A catalogue key still wins for names the catalogue owns, so existing links are unchanged. The caller names the slot; the class's own socket table still decides which attach point that means, so this is an instruction rather than a guess. Names are charset- and length-bounded and resolved only through the archive's index - never joined onto a path.
- **Character creation is a first-class part of the outfit.** Trove draws a head whether or not you own a hat, and `prefabs/custom_heads_service.binfab` is where that lives: nine **races** (Lady, Guy, Undead, Robot, Dragon, Ghost Pirate, Face Paint, Lunar Lancer, Headless), 47 heads and 5 eye sets split between them, and 141 hair styles shared by all - most credited to their community author, returned as `credit`. So `race`, `head`, `hair` and `eyes` are real slots with a catalogue behind them (and they still take a raw blueprint like any other). Leave `head`/`eyes` unset and the race's own default is drawn, matching what the game shows a player who never opened the customizer; pass `none` to leave it bare. Where each piece attaches is the game's answer, not a naming rule: an NPC prefab binds `c_p_head_male_01` to AP `head`, and three more bind `c_p_*_eyes` to AP `face` - which is why equipping a **`face` style replaces the eyes**, exactly as putting a mask on does in game.
- `GET /v1/dressing/races` → `{ items: [{ key, name, heads, eyes }] }`. `GET /v1/dressing/options?slot=head|eyes&race=` filters to that race's pieces; `slot=hair` is shared by every race.
- **Colour is hair and eyes only**, which is what Trove's own customizer offers: `hair_color`/`eye_color` take `#rrggbb` and tint those pieces' mask voxels (a head is authored in a real skin tone, so there is nothing to mask - you change skin by changing `race`). `GET /v1/dressing/palette` → the swatch grid the game's own picker shows, transcribed from it because the list is not in the shipped data; any `#rrggbb` is still accepted.
- A raw **weapon** blueprint carries no slot number, so `weapon_family=Melee|Bow|Gun|Staff|Spear|Fist` says which socket it fills. Omitted, it takes the family the class declares first - unambiguous for every class except the **Boomeranger**, which declares Bow before Melee, so name the family there.
- `GET /v1/dressing/options?slot=costume|hat|face|weapon[&class=&q=&offset=&limit=]` → `{ items: [{ key, name, slot, family, blueprint, prefab }], total, offset, limit }` - `class` is required for `costume` (a costume belongs to one class) and filters `weapon` to the families that class can hold, so an incompatible style is never offered. `q` searches the name.
- `GET /v1/dressing/outfit?class=[&costume=&race=&hat=&face=&weapon=&head=&hair=&eyes=&weapon_family=]` → `{ class, costume, race, hat, face, weapon, head, hair, eyes, dropped: [slot], issues: [{ slot, value, reason }] }` - normalises a selection without building anything: what a share link actually resolves to. An unknown/incompatible costume falls back to the class's first; a style this class has no socket for, a malformed name and a blueprint the archive doesn't have are all dropped and named, each with a `reason`: `unknown`, `no_socket`, `missing_asset` or `covered` (a full helmet replaces the hair and face style). **This is the endpoint to validate against when wiring up an embed** - it answers "is this name usable" without paying for the model.
- `GET /v1/dressing/model?class=[&costume=&race=&hat=&face=&weapon=&head=&hair=&eyes=&weapon_family=&fmt=json|bin]` → the assembled character as the web-viewer model payload (`{ voxel_scale, rig, parts, rest, animations }`) - the same shape `/v1/mods/hub/releases/{id}/assembled` returns, so the same viewer draws it. Built once per outfit, cached, gzipped and ETag'd. `fmt=bin` is the compact KVX1 container. Animation clips load lazily from `/v1/mods/hub/rigs/{skeleton}/anim/{name}`. Any slot that did not make it onto the model is named on the `X-Dressing-Dropped` response header (`hat=unknown,face=covered`) - a component is never omitted silently.
- `GET /v1/dressing/image?class=[&costume=&race=&hat=&face=&weapon=&head=&hair=&eyes=&weapon_family=&hair_color=&eye_color=&size=&az=&el=]` → a flat transparent **PNG** of the same character, rasterized server-side in the rest pose the viewer opens on. For a page that wants to *show* an outfit rather than let anyone turn it - a saved appearance on a profile, a thumbnail in a list - so it costs an `<img>` tag and no viewer, no WebGL and no scripts. Takes exactly the parameters `/model` does, so a link that opens the viewer becomes a picture by swapping one path segment. `size` is the square's side in pixels (32-512, default 256); `az`/`el` move the camera in degrees (default 30/8, a shallow three-quarter view). **The URL is the cache key** - the same selection is always the same picture - and the response is `immutable` for a year, so cache it as hard as you like. `X-Dressing-Dropped` is set here too.
- Embeddable: `/embed/viewer?dress=<class>:<costume>:<hat>:<face>:<weapon>:<head>:<hair>:<weapon_family>:<eyes>:<race>`, or - easier past ten positions - a query string in the same field (`dress=class%3Dknight%26race%3Dundead%26hair%3D…`) frames a dressed character on a partner site, alongside the existing `release`/`tmod`/`game` sources. Trailing fields are optional (an older five-field token still means what it did) and every slot takes a style stem or a blueprint name, e.g. `knight:knight_lvl3:equipment_hat_trovesaurus_01[ylva]:equipment_face_movember_01::c_p_knight_unfortunate_head`.
- Website page: **`/dressing-room`** (may be unpublished independently of the API - see above).

### BTT (`btt:read`) - BetterTroveTools releases (drives in-app update checks)

Relayed every 30 min from the GitHub releases of `AallynReed/BetterTroveTools` and cached in Mongo. Two channels: `release` (`prerelease=False`) and `beta` (`prerelease=True`). Three platforms detected by asset extension: `windows` (`.msi`/`.exe`, msi prioritized), `linux` (`.AppImage`/`.deb`/`.rpm`/`.tar.gz`), `android` (`.apk`).
- `GET /v1/btt/releases[?channel=release|beta&limit=50&offset=0]` → `{ channel, items: [BttRelease], count, total }`, BttRelease = `{ release_id, tag_name, name, body, html_url, prerelease, channel, published_at, fetched_at, assets:[{name, url, size, content_type, download_count}] }`.
- `GET /v1/btt/latest?channel=release` → `{ channel, platforms: { windows: PlatformLatest|null, linux: …, android: … } }`, PlatformLatest = `{ platform, release: BttReleaseMeta, assets:[Asset] }` (BttReleaseMeta = BttRelease minus `assets`). Each platform walks the channel newest-first to the first release that ships an asset for it - so a release without (say) a Windows build doesn't suppress Windows updates.
- `GET /v1/btt/latest/{platform}?channel=release` → one `PlatformLatest`. 404 if no release on that channel carries an asset for the platform yet.
- `GET /v1/btt/check?installed=<tag>&platform=<windows|linux|android>&channel=release` → `{ installed, channel, platform, update_available: bool, comparable: bool, latest: PlatformLatest|null }`. Server-side version comparison - the client just reads `update_available`. Accepts `v1.2.3` / `1.2.3` / `1.2.3-beta.1`; release > prerelease at the same numeric core. `comparable: false` means a tag couldn't be parsed (treat carefully). `latest: null` when no release on that channel ships an asset for the platform yet (returns false; doesn't 404).
- `GET /v1/btt/changelog[?limit_groups=&commits_per_group=]` → `{ repo, groups: [{version, commits: [{sha, short_sha, message, type, url}]}], rate_limited, fetched_at }`. Mirrors BTT's "Show changelog" button: commits from `GET /commits?per_page=100` grouped by git tag (`GET /tags`), newest first; commits since the latest tag live under `"Unreleased"`. `type` is the parsed conventional-commit prefix (feat/fix/docs/…) lowercased, or null. Cached server-side (30-min cadence) so users don't trip GitHub's 60/hr unauth rate limit. Returns an empty payload (not 404) before the first refresh completes.
- Everything above is mirrored from GitHub on a 30-min timer (`btt_releases_refresh_seconds`), so a freshly published release is invisible until the next cycle. `POST /admin/btt/refresh-releases` (superuser session, master panel → Config tab → **App releases**) pulls it immediately and returns `{ok, releases, changelog, downloads, latest:{"<channel>/<platform>": tag}, rate_limited, errors[]}`. Download counts ride on the assets, so they refresh with the same pull.

### Leaderboards (`leaderboards:read`) - Trove in-game leaderboards

Ingested from an external bot that periodically reads the game's `LeaderBot.cfg` file and POSTs the raw text to `/v1/leaderboards/insert`. The bot anchors each dump to the most recent 11:00 UTC reset (Trove's daily-reset hour); reads filter by that exact anchor. Entries older than 90 days are pruned on each insert (boards/metadata are kept forever). The `/insert` endpoint is **master-only** - it requires an API token belonging to a superuser account; the read endpoints take any token carrying `leaderboards:read`.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/timestamps[?limit=60]` → `{ items: [<unix_seconds>], count }` - recent dump anchors, newest first. Each value is a unix-seconds timestamp at 11:00 UTC.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards?created_at=<unix>` → `{ created_at, items: [Board], count }`, Board = `{ uuid, name_id, name, category_id, category, contest_type, reset_kind, player_board }`. `contest_type` is `"daily"`/`"weekly"`/`null` for THIS anchor; `reset_kind` describes the BOARD's cycle (`daily`/`weekly`/`default`); `player_board=false` for server-tally boards (1100, 21012). `created_at` may also be the 00:00 UTC alias for that day (normalized to 11:00).
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/{uuid}` → one `Board` plus its full `contests` list (`[{time, type}]`). 404 if no such board has ever been seen.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/{uuid}/entries?created_at=<unix>[&limit=100&offset=0]` → `{ uuid, created_at, items: [Entry], count, total, comparison }`. Entry = `{ rank, player_name, score, prev_rank, prev_score, rank_delta, score_delta, is_new }`. The deltas are day-over-day movement vs the previous trove-day's latest snapshot: `rank_delta = prev_rank - rank` (+ve = climbed), `score_delta = score - prev_score` (+ve = gained); `is_new=true` for a player with no prior-day position. Populated only when `comparison.comparable` is true - the board must NOT have reset between the two snapshots, so daily boards never carry day-over-day deltas, weekly boards skip across the Monday 11:00 UTC reset, and lifetime boards always compare. `comparison = { comparable, prev_anchor, reason }` (reason: `ok`/`no_prior_snapshot`/`crossed_reset`). `total` is the full row count (independent of the window). **Delve boards pack two readings into `score`.** On boards **2004 / 2014 / 2024** the value is `depth + 1 - sqrt(minutes / 180)`: the whole part is the depth reached, and the fraction is the run time, inverted so a faster run leaves a larger fraction and one descending sort ranks depth first, time second. Invert with `minutes = 180 * (1 - fraction)^2` (round the seconds - the square root means a ten-minute run comes back as 9.9997 minutes); a `.0000` fraction is the 180-minute cap. Those three ids are the whole rule - every other delve board carries a plain depth, and nothing in the payload distinguishes them, so do NOT infer a run time from a board's name. A difference of two packed scores is meaningless: compare `score` against `prev_score` and report either the depths or, at equal depth, the run-time difference. The `Fastest 3-Tier Clear` boards (`$Leaderboard_DelveThreeTier_{Challenge,Private,Public}Fastest`) instead carry minutes outright.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/players/{player_name}/history[?uuid=&limit=50]` → `{ player_name, items: [{ rank, player_name, score, leaderboard, created_at }], count }` - recent appearances of a player across boards (optionally filtered to one board), newest first. **Case-insensitive** exact match on `player_name` (Postgres `lower(name)`-indexed `player` lookup). **Hot-only**: the scan is floored at the hot/cold storage boundary (`leaderboards_pg_tier_after_days`, default 7d), so appearances older than that window aren't returned and the endpoint never reads cold-tiered partitions (the website `/site/…` proxy and the signed-in dashboard keep their deeper reach). (The showcase site's `/site/…` proxy of this also attaches the same `rank_delta`/`score_delta` per row; the public endpoint leaves those null.)
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/players/{player_name}/profile` → `{ player_name, verified, summary: { boards_appeared, appearances, best_rank, best_rank_board_uuid, best_rank_board_name, latest_anchor }, recent: [{ player_name, leaderboard, board_name, rank, score, created_at, prev_rank, prev_score, rank_delta, score_delta, is_new }] }` - **tokenless** public profile aggregate (recent appearances enriched with board names + day-over-day deltas, plus a summary). `verified=true` when a site account has claimed AND been master-approved for this name (ties to the manual claim flow). Unknown names return an empty `recent`, not a 404. **Hot-only**: the `recent` window is floored at the hot/cold storage boundary (`leaderboards_pg_tier_after_days`, default 7d) so the endpoint never reads cold-tiered partitions - the `boards`/summary block still spans all history (it's the always-hot `player_board_agg` aggregate). Powers `/player/<name>` and a future bot `/rank` deep-link.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/players/{player_name}/boards` → `{ player_name, summary: { boards_appeared, appearances, best_rank, best_rank_board_uuid, best_rank_board_name, top10_count, top100_count, latest_anchor }, boards: [{ leaderboard, board_name, category, best_rank, latest_rank, latest_score, appearances, first_seen, last_seen }] }` - **tokenless** per-leaderboard aggregate read straight from the materialised `player_board_agg` table: one row per board the player has ever appeared on (best rank ever, current rank/score, capture count, first/last seen), best boards first, plus a roll-up summary. Leaner/cheaper than `/profile` - an O(boards) aggregate read with **no** rename reconstruction, alt-cluster detection, or last-played scan (use `/profile` when you want those + the recent per-capture rows). **Case-insensitive** exact name match; unknown names return an empty `boards`, not a 404. Public tokenless/token pattern: sending a token carrying `leaderboards:read` earns the higher per-token rate limit over the stricter per-IP anon budget.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/{uuid}/health` → `{ uuid, name, category, reset_kind, anchor, prev_anchor, comparable, comparison_reason, population, sample_size, leader_share, p1_pn_ratio, gini, turnover_rate, new_entrants, median_score_gain, median_score_gain_pct }` - board health from the latest snapshot vs the previous trove-day. **Competitiveness** (always present): `leader_share` = #1 score / Σ(top-N), `p1_pn_ratio` = #1 / last-in-sample, `gini` = 0 (even) … →1 (one player dominates). **Turnover + score inflation** (`turnover_rate`/`new_entrants`/`median_score_gain[_pct]`) are day-over-day and **null when not comparable** (`comparable=false`: a reset crossed, or no prior snapshot - same comparability rule as `/entries`).
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/{uuid}/history[?days=7&top=5]` and `GET /v1/leaderboards/players/{player_name}/series[?days=7]` → chart-ready timeseries. Series points carry `{ created_at, rank, score, synthetic }`. **Reset-zero injection**: on daily/weekly boards the server inserts synthetic points at every reset moment falling between two real captures - one "hold-flat" point at `R − 1s` carrying the pre-reset score, plus a `score=0` point at the reset `R` itself - so the chart shows an honest cliff drop instead of a smoothed descent. Lifetime boards (`reset_kind` ∈ `default`/`none`) skip injection. Renderers should keep synthetic points in the line path but suppress hover dots / tooltips on them (`synthetic=true`). **Gaps**: a series can be missing at an anchor (player dropped out of the top-`top`, or that capture is absent entirely) - joining straight across draws a trend nobody measured, so a renderer should split the line at any step wider than the capture cadence (median anchor delta) and stroke the missing stretch dashed/dimmed. The site charts do this via `BTTUtil.segmentGaps`. Resets are at midnight UTC−11 (i.e. **11:00 UTC**); weekly boards reset on Monday at that time. Real captures always carry `synthetic=false`. **Hot-only (player `/series`)**: `days` on the per-player `/players/{name}/series` is capped at the hot/cold storage boundary (`leaderboards_pg_tier_after_days`, default 7d), so a larger requested window is silently clamped and the trajectory never reaches cold-tiered partitions (the per-board `/{uuid}/history` is unaffected - it's served from the warm cache). **Fast path**: `/{uuid}/history` only queries the top-`top` players' rows (three indexed Postgres queries - distinct anchors, the latest anchor's top-N, then those players' trajectories - NOT the whole board's window), and the result is served from a Redis read-through cache whose default `7d/top=5` payload the warmer pre-computes for EVERY board on each ingest, so the per-board chart paints instantly.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/cheaters` → `{ players: [{ player_name, confidence, leaderboards: [{ uuid, name, category, contest_type, rank, score, evidence: [{ type, summary, measurements, confidence }] }] }], clusters: [{ stem, label, method, corroborated_by, member_count, members, members_truncated, board_count, boards: [{ uuid, name, category, contest_type, members, member_names, score_min, score_max, spread, rank_min, rank_max, matching_hours, avg_hourly_gain }], confidence, summary, measurements }], clusters_boards_scanned, computed_at, anchor, method, config, total_flagged, boards_analyzed, boards_excluded, analyzed_boards: [{ uuid, name, category, reset_kind, contest_type, entries }], excluded_boards: [{ uuid, name, category, reset_kind, contest_type, reason: "admin_excluded"|"below_min_size", entries? }] }` - **tokenless**. The `analyzed_boards` / `excluded_boards` arrays detail exactly which boards the run scanned vs skipped (sorted by category+name); `reset_kind` reflects the admin override (so a board pinned to `none` shows as lifetime regardless of the hardcoded mapping). `excluded_boards.reason` distinguishes operator opt-out from below-min-size skips. **Counts are derived from the lists** - `boards_analyzed = len(analyzed_boards)` and `boards_excluded = count of reason="admin_excluded"`. Flags statistically anomalous play on the latest captured anchor. Runs three independent per-player checks (in `players`) plus a group-shaped alt-cluster check (in `clusters`). **Score outlier** - `log10`-transformed Modified Z-score against the **elite cohort** (top 5% or top 50, whichever larger) of the board, NOT the full population. Trove leaderboards are heavy-tailed (top players score 10-100× the median), so a naive full-board MAD-Z falsely flags every dedicated top player; using the cohort + log-transform restricts the check to "anomalous *among the top players*". Default threshold: 5.0. Capped boards (top-5 scores tied) are skipped entirely. Only the top half of the cohort is checked. **Rank-gap** - score drop from rank N to N+1 vs the typical between-rank gap on the same board (10× cutoff). **Velocity** - score-gain rate vs the board's peer p95 rate, using the player's previous historical capture (10× cutoff). **Weekly uptime** (`sustained_velocity` evidence) - a WEEK-long pattern, not just the last hour: a player whose score rose in ≥ `cheaters_weekly_uptime_fraction` (default 0.85) of the captures since the weekly reset. No human plays 85%+ of every hour for days - that's a no-sleep bot, which the per-hour velocity check can't see (each hour looks normal alone). Only applies once ≥48 captures have elapsed; computed from the same week data the cluster pass loads (no extra queries). **Reset-cycle aware**: for daily/weekly boards (cadence on the `reset_kind` field) the previous-anchor lookup is bounded to the same reset cycle - comparing a score across a reset boundary would otherwise produce spurious flags as "starting fresh and grinding hard" looks like an extreme velocity vs a baseline that mixes pre- and post-reset rates. **Alt-cluster** (the only *group*-shaped check; emitted in the separate `clusters` array, NOT as per-player evidence) - families of similarly-named accounts (`anana1 … anana20`, `Aan_1 … Aan_7`) sitting at near-identical scores. Names are grouped by a normalised **stem** (trailing digits/separators stripped, then leet/number-substitution folded so `Dr4g0n`≈`dragon`) plus a small **edit-distance** merge for typo'd variants; per board the **densest near-score subset** (≥ `cheaters_cluster_min_size` accounts within `cheaters_cluster_score_band_pct`) is kept, then the same family is merged across boards. None of the per-player checks can see this - each alt is unremarkable alone; only the family is anomalous. Cluster `confidence` (capped at 0.95) folds three signals: **closeness** (tightest board's spread vs the band), **size** (ramps to full at `cheaters_cluster_size_full` accounts), and **board count** (`1 − 0.5^boards`); the `measurements` dict exposes each sub-term. Every cluster carries a `method`: **co_movement** is the PRIMARY, name-agnostic signal - accounts whose hourly score GAINS move in lockstep across the captures since the last weekly reset. Per board it keeps only the top-percentile gainers each hour (`cheaters_comovement_gain_percentile`, so a crowd at a common rate drops out), bands each hour's survivors into tolerance groups (`cheaters_comovement_gain_tolerance_pct`, a sorted sweep so a hair's-width gain difference can't straddle a fixed-bucket edge and split a real ring), and links two accounts only when their shared (hour, band) cells are BOTH ≥ `cheaters_comovement_min_matching_hours` AND ≥ `cheaters_comovement_min_match_ratio` of the rarer account's active hours (a fraction, not an absolute count - so a few coincidental matches over a long week can't chain the hardcore-grinder crowd into one giant false ring). Each connected group is then peeled to its dense core (`cheaters_comovement_min_density`, so a loose transitive chain collapses while a near-clique ring survives) before merging across boards by member overlap; co-movement confidence (capped 0.97) folds matching-hour count + group size, and those boards carry `matching_hours`/`avg_hourly_gain` instead of the score-range fields. **schedule** is a name-agnostic SCHEDULE-correlation producer: accounts active/idle in the same hours since the weekly reset (Jaccard of active-hour sets ≥ `cheaters_schedule_min_similarity`, ≥ `cheaters_schedule_min_active_hours` active hours, "always-on" accounts excluded as non-distinctive) - catches alts that grind DIFFERENT content but play together, which co-movement (gain-magnitude) misses; weak alone, so low base confidence unless corroborated. **name_stem** is the name+near-score method above; **both** marks a group flagged by several signals. **FUSION**: the producers' clusters (name_stem + co_movement + schedule) are merged by member overlap, every signal is re-evaluated on each merged group (co-movement, schedule cohesion, shared name stem, board-footprint Jaccard ≥ `cheaters_footprint_min_jaccard`), and the agreeing signals are listed in `corroborated_by` - confidence is the strongest single-signal value PLUS `cheaters_fusion_corroboration_bonus` per EXTRA independent signal (capped 0.98). The whole point: a group flagged by co-movement AND schedule AND name is far more certain than one. The history pass is windowed to the current week, candidate-limited (top `cheaters_comovement_candidate_top_n` by rank per board), run off the event loop, and throttled to `cheaters_comovement_recompute_seconds` (cached by weekly-window, reused across warm cycles). Each per-player evidence carries a per-check `confidence` (sigmoid on `magnitude / threshold`, 0.5 at the threshold, capped by per-check ceilings reflecting empirical false-positive rates: velocity=0.99, rank_gap=0.85, score_outlier=0.60); each player carries an overall `confidence` aggregated as max-within-board, noisy-OR across boards, with a diversity cap (if only one check type fires, overall confidence is limited to that type's ceiling - so a player anomalous-by-static-rank on 10 boards but normal-velocity still caps at 0.60 because score_outlier alone is too noisy to claim certainty without corroboration). Server-side cached in-process for `cheaters_cache_ttl_seconds` (default 1800s) AND pre-computed by a background warmer at app boot + on the same TTL cadence, so callers never wait for the per-board scan. All thresholds (`cheaters_z_threshold`, `cheaters_velocity_multiplier`, `cheaters_elite_cohort_pct`, `cheaters_min_board_size`), the alt-cluster knobs (`cheaters_cluster_min_size`, `cheaters_cluster_score_band_pct`, `cheaters_cluster_max_edit_distance`, `cheaters_cluster_size_full`), the co-movement knobs (`cheaters_comovement_candidate_top_n` [0 disables], `cheaters_comovement_min_hourly_gain`, `cheaters_comovement_gain_percentile`, `cheaters_comovement_gain_tolerance_pct`, `cheaters_comovement_min_matching_hours`, `cheaters_comovement_min_match_ratio`, `cheaters_comovement_min_density`, `cheaters_comovement_min_group_size`, `cheaters_comovement_max_cell_accounts`, `cheaters_comovement_recompute_seconds`), the schedule + fusion knobs (`cheaters_schedule_min_active_hours`, `cheaters_schedule_min_similarity`, `cheaters_fusion_corroboration_bonus`, `cheaters_footprint_min_jaccard`), the weekly-uptime knob (`cheaters_weekly_uptime_fraction`), the TTL, and the two INDEPENDENT board blacklists - `cheaters_excluded_board_uuids` (per-player checks) and `cheaters_cluster_excluded_board_uuids` (alt-cluster check) - are runtime-tunable from the master admin panel. `clusters_boards_scanned` reports how many boards the cluster pass examined (its own blacklist + min-size, distinct from `boards_analyzed`). The response echoes the active `config` and `boards_excluded` count so a flag is reproducible.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/renames[?limit=50&offset=0]` → `{ renames: [{ id, from_name, to_name, from_anchor, to_anchor, confidence, matched_boards, evidence: { gap_seconds, boards: [{ uuid, name, score_from, score_to, drift_pct }], terms: { board_term, tightness, exclusivity, rarity, mean_drift_pct, confidence, … }, summary }, method_version, created_at }], total, limit, offset, enabled, method_version }` - **tokenless**. Reconstructed player **name changes**, most-recent-first (by `to_anchor`, the capture the new name appeared in). Trove leaderboards carry no stable player id (a rename mints a brand-new `player` row), so a rename is inferred from behaviour: between two **adjacent** captures within `renames_max_gap_seconds` (default 5400s = 1.5h - wider gaps let scores drift + the population churn, so they're skipped), a name that **vanished** while a NEW name **appeared** carrying the same **lifetime-board** score fingerprint. The fingerprint uses ONLY non-resetting boards (`reset_kind` ∈ `default`/`none` - Trove Mastery, Geode Mastery, Power Rank, lifetime stat boards; scores there carry over a rename unchanged and never reset), which makes the whole detection **reset-immune by construction** - a pair straddling an 11:00-UTC daily/weekly reset can never look like a rename. **Conservative matcher**: a rename is emitted only when the fingerprint matches on ≥ `renames_min_boards` (default 2) lifetime boards with near-equal scores (allowing a small positive drift ≤ `renames_score_drift_pct`, default 2% - a renamed player keeps grinding, so the new score may be slightly higher but never lower), the old/new names are a **mutual** best match (each is the other's top candidate - no double-assignment), and the match is **unambiguous** (no runner-up candidate of equal board-overlap). Anything ambiguous is dropped, not guessed. `confidence` (capped 0.97) folds **board_term** (`1 − 0.5^matched`), **tightness** (how far below the drift tolerance the carries sit - exact carry-over → 1), **exclusivity** (runner-up margin), and **rarity** (fraction of matched boards whose score cell held exactly one candidate); the `terms` dict exposes each sub-term. Entries scoring below `renames_min_score` (default 1000) are ignored as too low-entropy to fingerprint. Detected **live** by the leaderboards warmer on the newest adjacent pair each ingest, and rebuildable across the whole archive via the master backfill below. Records persist in a `player_rename` table; the whole feature is gated by the `feature_leaderboard_renames_enabled` master switch (OFF → this returns 404 and `enabled:false` on the `/site` proxy). `Cache-Control: public, max-age=renames_cache_ttl_seconds` (default 300).
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/renames/{name}` → `{ query, current_name, aliases: [...], edges: [<RenameEvent>…], rename_count }` - **tokenless**. The full rename **chain** touching `name`: rename edges are walked in BOTH directions (case-insensitive), so an identity that renamed several times (A→B→C) returns its whole timeline ordered oldest→newest, the set of `aliases`, and the `current_name` (the newest `to_name`).
- `POST /v1/leaderboards/renames-backfill[?clear_first=false]` - **master only**. Walk the WHOLE stored capture history over every adjacent pair within `renames_max_gap_seconds` and (re)detect renames into `player_rename`. Reset-safe (lifetime-board fingerprint) and gap-gated (multi-hour outage gaps skipped); idempotent - safe to re-run. `clear_first=true` wipes recorded renames first, then rebuilds. Returns **202**; runs in the BACKGROUND (single-flight guarded, slides each pair's later fingerprint into the next pair's earlier one so each anchor loads ~once). Poll `GET /v1/leaderboards/renames-backfill-status` → `{ running, total, done, detected, skipped_gap, last_anchor, lifetime_boards, recorded_renames, … }` for live progress.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/duplicates[?limit=50&offset=0&kind=same_name|case]` → `{ duplicates: [{ name, kind, verdict, boards, max_occurrences, spellings: [...], first_anchor, last_anchor, evidence: { lookback_days, boards: [{ uuid, name, occurrences, series: [{ slot, captures, first_anchor, last_anchor, first_score, last_score, last_rank, moved, frozen }] }], summary }, method_version, updated_at }], total, current, latest_anchor, limit, offset, enabled, method_version }` - **tokenless**. Names that do NOT resolve to a single player, still-current first then widest blast radius. Trove's dump carries no player id (only `rank;name;score`), so identity is keyed by name - and that breaks two ways, both reported here. `kind='same_name'`: the game's OWN capture lists the identical spelling **twice on the same board**, at two ranks with two scores, and both rows resolve to one `player` row. `kind='case'`: two spellings differing only in capitalisation (`Robot` / `robot`) fold into one `name_lower` key, merging two accounts - detected at INGEST from the raw staging rows, because after the entries are stored that evidence is gone. A name hit by both is `kind='both'` and matches either `?kind=` filter. The evidence splits each board's co-existing rows into per-identity **series** (see the split note below) and reports whether each one `moved` or is `frozen` over `duplicates_lookback_days` (default 7). `verdict` is DESCRIPTIVE and never asserts which identity is the real player (nothing in the data supports that): `one_live` (exactly one series still moving, the rest frozen - what a leftover leaderboard row looks like), `multi_live` (2+ still moving - separate active identities sharing a name), `all_idle` (nothing moved in the window, undecidable), `case_only`, `not_analysed` (dated by the archive backfill but never measured - it only reads the series for names still in the newest capture, since an older window is cold-tiered and costs ~35s apiece; `evidence` is `{}` and this is NOT a finding of "nothing moved"). Detected **live** by the leaderboards warmer on the newest capture each ingest, and datable across the whole archive via the master backfill below. Records persist in a `player_duplicate` table (one row per name); gated by the `feature_leaderboard_duplicates_enabled` master switch (OFF → 404 here and `enabled:false` on the `/site` proxy). Knobs: `duplicates_*` (master panel, `duplicates` category). `Cache-Control: public, max-age=duplicates_cache_ttl_seconds` (default 300).
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/duplicates/{name}` → `{ query, found, enabled, name, kind, verdict, boards, max_occurrences, spellings, first_anchor, last_anchor, evidence, method_version, updated_at }` - **tokenless**. Whether ONE name resolves to more than one identity, case-insensitive. `found:false` is the normal answer and means the name is unambiguous. When true, treat that player's LIFETIME aggregate (best rank, appearances, totals) as covering more than one identity - the per-board evidence separates the score lines, but the aggregate cannot be split retroactively.
- `POST /v1/leaderboards/duplicates-backfill[?clear_first=false]` - **master only**. Walk EVERY stored capture and (re)detect duplicated names into `player_duplicate`, folding each anchor into the record so `first_anchor` dates the real start of the duplication (the live pass only ever sees the newest capture, so it can't). Idempotent; `clear_first=true` wipes first. Returns **202**, runs in the BACKGROUND (single-flight guarded). Poll `GET /v1/leaderboards/duplicates-backfill-status` → `{ running, total, done, detected, last_anchor, recorded_duplicates, … }`. NOTE: `case` groups are captured at ingest from the raw dump, so this rebuilds `same_name` groups only - a `clear_first` run drops case history until new captures land or the backlog is re-ingested.
- **Per-identity series split (applies everywhere, not gated by the flag).** Because a duplicated name has two rows at the SAME anchor on the same board, any naive per-player read interleaves two people: the chart drew both values at each timestamp as one vertical sawtooth, and day-over-day deltas compared a row against the other identity's previous value (producing multi-million-point phantom gains). `GET /v1/leaderboards/players/{name}/series` now emits **one entry per identity** - each carries `slot` (0-based, stable, ordered by first appearance) and `slots` (how many identities that board resolved to), with `duplicate_boards` on the payload - and `…/history` rows carry the same `slot`/`slots`. Rows are linked capture-to-capture by score continuity: each open series predicts its next value from its own recent rate and the assignment minimising total miss wins, with score DROPS penalised. Sorting by score was rejected (a frozen leftover row can sit ABOVE the live one, so the lines swap when the live one overtakes it), as was minimising raw score movement (degenerate - when every row rises, total movement is identical for every pairing). `slots` is 1 for every unambiguous player, so existing consumers are unaffected. The profile's `last_played` is likewise computed per slot; without it the lag alternated between the two rows and the player read as permanently active.
- `GET /v1/leaderboards/records` → `{ trove_mastery, geode_mastery, power_rank }` - **tokenless**. The current in-game *ceiling* for each stat, read off the rank-1 holder of the relevant **lifetime** board (these never reset, so their #1 is an all-time record). `trove_mastery` (board 1) and `geode_mastery` (board 20) are `{ points, level, points_into_level, points_to_next_level, player_name, anchor }` - the boards store a running Mastery **points** total, and `level` runs that total through the in-game points→level curve (levels 2-5 cost 25pts, 6-10 cost 50, 11-20 cost 75, 21-300 cost 100, 301+ cost `150 + ceil((level-300)*0.5)`), with `points_into_level`/`points_to_next_level` showing progress into the current level. **Geode is soft-capped at level 100 in-game**, so its `level` is clamped there and it carries extra fields `{ level_cap: 100, uncapped_level, capped }` - `uncapped_level` is what the points would reach without the cap (e.g. `100` vs a true `143`), `capped=true` when the two differ. `power_rank` is `{ value, board_uuid, player_name, anchor }` - the single highest Power Rank across all 17 per-class boards (1000-1016); `value` is stored directly (no level conversion) and `board_uuid` says which class board it came from. Any of the three is `null` only if that board has never been ingested. Refreshes at most once per daily dump (11:00 UTC); `Cache-Control: public, max-age=900`.
- `POST /v1/leaderboards/insert[?timestamp=<unix>]` (multipart `file`) - **master only**. Submit the raw cfg text as a multipart `file` field. Idempotent for a given anchor: re-running the same dump on the same timestamp converges. `timestamp` is optional and only used for back-fills; omit it for a normal scrape. Returns **202 Accepted** immediately with `{ accepted, bytes, message }` - the parse + persist (sub-second `COPY` load on a full dump) runs in the BACKGROUND so the bot's client isn't held open and timed out; the resulting `{ boards, entries, cleared_before_insert, created_at }` counts (or any parse/DB error, as `success:false`) are written to the master ingest log when processing finishes. **Full-history storage in PostgreSQL** (a dedicated DB, separate from the app's Mongo): the `entry` table is RANGE-partitioned by anchor (one partition per trove-day, 11:00-UTC boundary), so old data is just old partitions - no hot/cold collection split. Partitioned-parent indexes `(board_uuid, anchor, rank)` and `(player_id, anchor)` keep both board-at-time and player-over-time reads O(index seek) at any age; player names are normalised into a `player` dimension table. `leaderboards_hot_retention_days` (default 3 days; runtime-tunable from the master admin panel) now just controls how many recent days the warmer pre-warms / the page surfaces. Use `/timestamps?limit=` to enumerate ALL stored anchors (deduped). **Archive rate limit**: queries with a `?created_at=` older than `leaderboards_archive_query_threshold_days` (default 3 - bot captures hourly, so a 3-day window already covers ~72 anchors of "recent" data) pay a SECOND, tighter per-token bucket (default 10 req/min) on top of the standard cap - surfaced via `X-RateLimit-Archive-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` response headers. Applies to `/v1/leaderboards?created_at=` and `/v1/leaderboards/{uuid}/entries?created_at=`; queries within the threshold pay only the standard cap. The threshold is runtime-tunable from the master admin panel. **Ingest cooldown**: API-token submissions are additionally capped at `ingest_cooldown_max` per `ingest_cooldown_window_seconds` (default 1 per 300s) per token per endpoint - exceeding returns 429 with `Retry-After`. Session-JWT calls (portal "Manual cfg ingest") bypass this so master back-fills aren't blocked. **Completeness guard**: a LIVE capture is REJECTED (not stored, ack'd but flagged `success:false` in the ingest log with the reason) when it arrives materially incomplete vs the previous good capture - the in-game scrape can return a short dump when the leaderboards are briefly down or crash mid-run. Detection is by board PRESENCE (id set): reject when more than `capture_max_missing_boards` (default 1) boards present last capture are absent now, or (secondary) when a board present in both COLLAPSED below `capture_collapse_frac` (default 0.5) of its previous entry count. Gated to non-reset windows (board rotation / daily zeroing at a reset is legitimate) and skipped when the previous capture had < `capture_min_prev_boards` boards. Rejecting is deliberate: storing a short dump poisons every delta consumer (activity, cheater velocity, renames, day-over-day deltas) because players merely absent from it read as "newly appeared / active"; dropping it makes the hour a clean time-gap that all of them already bridge over. The raw dump is still saved to the backlog for audit / manual re-ingest. The guard is SKIPPED on `?backfill=true` bulk re-seeds (trusts the operator). All knobs (`capture_completeness_enabled`, `capture_max_missing_boards`, `capture_collapse_frac`, `capture_min_prev_boards`) are runtime-tunable (master panel, `ingest_quality` category).
- `POST /v1/leaderboards/delete-anchor?anchor=<unix>[&recompute=true]` - **master only**. Delete every entry for ONE capture - purge a bad capture that slipped in before the guard (or was force-ingested). The hour becomes a clean time-gap that activity / cheater / rename / delta calculations bridge over. With `recompute` (default) the activity history is rebuilt in the background (the affected window recomputes as a gap, so any spike it caused disappears) and the leaderboards warmer is kicked. Returns `{ deleted, anchor, entries_deleted, recompute }`.

### Activity (`activity:read`) - free/public Trove player-activity estimates

Lower-bound active-player counts derived from the leaderboard captures (distinct top-N players whose score rose between captures). **Public / tokenless** - a token carrying `activity:read` just earns the wider per-token budget. Powers the showcase `/activity` ("Player Activity") page via the same-origin `/site` proxies, but documented + stable for third-party dashboards / wikis too. All cached for `cheaters_cache_ttl_seconds`. (These replaced the old `/v1/misc/activity*` and `/v1/leaderboards/activity*` copies.)
- `GET /v1/activity/current` → `{ estimate, estimate_24h, estimate_7d, window_24h_start, window_7d_start, span_24h_hours, span_7d_hours, window_start, window_end, duration_hours, by_board:[{uuid,name,category,active_players}], boards_analyzed, methodology, computed_at }` - lower-bound distinct active players between the two most recent captures: a player whose score ROSE on any board vs the previous capture, or who newly appears with a non-zero score (`score > prev`, absent-previous treated as 0). No score ceilings, no board filters; a reset drop isn't a rise. `estimate_24h` / `estimate_7d` are distinct-active rollups over the last 24h / 7d - the distinct UNION of each capture's active set in the period. Each capture's set is MATERIALIZED once in an `activity_active` table, so the rollups are an indexed `COUNT(DISTINCT)` over the windows in range - the true union, MONOTONIC (`7d ⊇ 24h ⊇ 1h`), no re-scan. `null` until an earlier anchor exists; `span_*_hours` = the window actually covered. `estimate` is `null` until two captures exist.
- `GET /v1/activity/history?days=7` (1–30) → `{ days, window_start, window_end, methodology, points:[{window_end, window_start, duration_hours, estimate, estimate_per_hour}] }` - time-series, one point per consecutive capture pair. `estimate_per_hour = estimate / duration_hours` is the value a chart should plot (a missed capture makes a window span 2-3h and inflates the raw `estimate`; the per-hour rate normalises it). Persisted per ingest, survives restarts.
- `GET /v1/activity/series?period=7d` (period ∈ `1d`/`7d`/`1m` - longer ranges were removed) → `{ period, bucket_seconds, window_start, window_end, points:[{t, active, avg, peak, samples}], peak:{t, active}|null, low:{t, active}|null, average, latest, methodology }` - downsampled activity-level series; each point is a fixed time bucket sized to the period (hourly for `1d`/`7d`, daily for `1m`). `active` is the plotted value with EXTREMES PRESERVED: the single busiest bucket in the range plots its true max (at the exact peak capture), the single quietest its true min, every other bucket its `avg` - so a coarse wide-timeframe bucket never flattens the real peak into an average. `avg` is always the bucket mean; `peak` its busiest hour. Top-level `peak`/`low` are the period's true max/min (timestamped at the actual capture); `average`/`latest` summarise the period. Buckets whose windows span a missed capture are DROPPED, not zero-filled, so `points` can have holes - a renderer should judge contiguity on the bucket index (`floor(t / bucket_seconds)`, since `t` is the bucket's centroid/extreme, not its start) and draw the missing stretches dashed rather than as a straight climb. Backs the `/activity` page charts.
- `POST /v1/activity/backfill[?total_days=400&chunk_days=14&force=false&reset=false]` - **master only**. Seeds the `/series` history from the stored Postgres captures so the multi-period charts have data predating the hourly forward-fill. `total_days=0` rebuilds ALL stored history (no lower bound); else the trailing N days. Returns **202** + runs in the BACKGROUND, STREAMING one capture's entries at a time (a 1-deep sliding window over consecutive anchor pairs), so peak memory stays at ~one capture regardless of range - the naive "load the whole range into one dict" approach OOMs on dense hourly data. Coverage capped by how far the stored entries reach; `force=false` skips already-computed windows. (`chunk_days` is accepted for compatibility but unused now that the load streams.) The per-hour series skips windows that span a missed capture; the gap cutoff is derived from the **median capture cadence** (not a hardcoded 1h), so a non-hourly or jittery archive isn't dropped wholesale - the backfill logs `median_interval_hours` / `gap_threshold_hours` / `gap_skipped` for diagnosis. **`reset=true` is destructive**: it first DELETES every stored estimate, then recomputes the whole range from scratch (implies `force`) - use it to flush miscalculations from older runs. The `activity_estimate` table is fully derived data, so nothing irreplaceable is lost; the charts just read empty until the rebuild lands (`reset_deleted` count is logged).

### Class activity (`activity:read`) - free/public per-class Trove activity

Per-Trove-class version of player activity, from the **Effort (`4000+i`)** leaderboards: `class_index = board_uuid % 1000` maps to the game's class release order (0=Knight … 17=Solarion, verified against the stored board names). Paragon (`5000+i`) is **excluded as ambiguous** — neither counted nor filtered on. A class is "active" in a window when a player's score rose (or first appears) on its Effort board (this score-rose measure drives the time-series `/series`; the donut `/current` instead counts players simply *present* on the Effort board in the latest snapshot — see each endpoint below). Effort boards reset weekly (Mon 11:00 UTC) so windows crossing the reset are unmeasurable (no point). **Two views in every payload:** RAW counts everyone; CLEAN (the `/class-activity` page default, "established", `*_clean` fields) keeps only players who, snapshot at the window end, clear ALL THREE floors — Power Rank (`1000+i` board) ≥ `class_activity_power_rank_threshold` (default **25000**), Effort (`4000+i`) ≥ `class_activity_effort_threshold` (default **50**) and score on the global XP stats board (`21005`) ≥ `class_activity_xp_threshold` (default **2,000,000**) — all three master-tunable runtime settings (set any to 0 to drop that gate); this filters new characters + alts. A player missing from a captured XP board reads as 0 (filtered, same as the other floors), but an XP board absent from a capture entirely degrades the XP floor to a no-op for that window (it never zeroes the clean view). `clean` is `null` where unmeasurable (no Power Rank snapshot). Same `activity:read` scope, same `/site/leaderboards/class-activity/*` proxy family, powers the `/class-activity` page (multi-line chart with an Established/All toggle + player-share donut).
- `GET /v1/class-activity/current` → `{ window_start, window_end, duration_hours, total_active, total_active_clean, total_effort_added, total_effort_added_clean, power_rank_threshold, effort_threshold, xp_threshold, classes:[{class_index, name, icon, active_players, share, active_players_clean, share_clean, effort_added, effort_added_clean}], methodology, computed_at }` - **a direct headcount of the LATEST snapshot, NOT the activity pipeline**: per class, the players *present* on its Effort board at the newest capture (Paragon excluded; no score-rose step), for BOTH views (`share`/`share_clean` each sum to 1 over their measurable classes). `effort_added`/`effort_added_clean` (+ the `total_*` rollups) are the Effort added to each board in the **latest hour** (this capture vs the previous; Σ positive per-player gains, per view; `null` when there's no previous capture or the pair crosses the weekly reset). `share` is share-of-players: a player on N classes counts in each, NOT distinct players. `*_clean` is `null` where the clean view is unmeasurable (no Power Rank board in the snapshot). `window_start`=`window_end`=snapshot anchor; `duration_hours` is null. `classes` sorted by the clean view desc (None last). (Powers the page's player-share donut; `/series` below stays activity-based.)
- `GET /v1/class-activity/series?period=7d` (period ∈ `1d`…`all`) → `{ period, bucket_seconds, window_start, window_end, power_rank_threshold, effort_threshold, xp_threshold, buckets:[t,…], classes:[{class_index, name, icon, values:[float|null,…], values_clean:[float|null,…]}], methodology }` - per-class bucketed series with a SHARED x-axis (`buckets`); each class's `values` (raw) and `values_clean` (PR+Effort+XP-filtered) align to it (avg active/hr per bucket on the Effort board, `null` where that view had no measurable window in the bucket). Peak-preserving like `/v1/activity/series`: each class's busiest bucket plots its true max instead of the bucket average, so a coarse wide-timeframe bucket still shows the real peak (short ranges are unchanged; only the peak is preserved per class, not the min). Same bucket sizing as `/v1/activity/series`. **Two kinds of hole** a renderer must not draw through: a `null` in a class's `values` (that view had no measurable window there - e.g. a window crossing the weekly reset), and a bucket missing from `buckets` entirely (no captures at all). Both are caught by judging contiguity on the bucket key (`floor(bucket_t / bucket_seconds)`, since `buckets` carries centroids) and stroking the missing stretch dashed rather than as a straight rise.
- `POST /v1/class-activity/backfill[?total_days=400&force=false&reset=false]` - **master only**. Seeds the per-class history (raw + clean; `class_activity_estimate` table) from stored captures; same memory-safe streaming as the activity backfill, loading the 18 Effort boards + 18 Power Rank boards (+ the XP board `21005` when that floor is on) per anchor. `total_days=0` = all history; `reset=true` wipes first (implies force). **202** + background. Run after changing any clean-view floor to apply it across history (the warmer applies it to the latest window each capture automatically).

### Giveaways (`giveaways:read`) - free/public Trove community giveaways

**Public / tokenless** - a token carrying `giveaways:read` just earns the wider per-token budget. The showcase `/giveaways` page is the main consumer (via the same-origin `/site/giveaways` proxy); this is the documented, stable API surface. (Entering a giveaway is a signed-in site-user action, not part of the public API.)
- `GET /v1/giveaways/ongoing` → `[{ id, title, description, prize_name, status, starts_at, ends_at, entry_count, winner_username }]` - currently-OPEN giveaways (accepting entries), soonest to end first. `status` is `"open"` for all of these; `winner_username` is always `null` (winners only appear after a draw) and the prize code is NEVER exposed. Use `entry_count` to compute odds (`1 / entry_count`) and `ends_at` for the countdown. Cached 30s.
- `GET /v1/giveaways/upcoming` → same shape - SCHEDULED giveaways not yet open, soonest-starting first. `status` is `"scheduled"`; `entry_count` is 0 until `starts_at`. Cached 30s.
- `GET /v1/giveaways/ended[?days=7]` (days 1–30) → same shape - giveaways that ENDED in the last `days` days (default 7), most-recently-ended first. `status` is `"drawn"` (had a winner - see `winner_username`) or `"closed"` (no entrants); cancelled giveaways are excluded. Cached 30s.

### Market (`market:read`) - Trove marketplace listings

Ingested from the same bot that submits leaderboards. Every hour or so the bot reads the game's `GrainusMod.cfg` and POSTs the raw text to `/v1/market/insert`. Each line is `<uuid>;<name>;<type>;<stack>;<price>` with the UUID v1 of the in-game listing. Listings are stored in **Postgres** (`market_listing` table, the same DB as leaderboards): the UUID is the primary key, its timestamp decodes into `created_at` (when the player posted the listing), and `last_seen` is bumped on every re-scrape via UPSERT (so re-seeing the same listing never duplicates). Only items on the interest list (`gamedata/market_items.json`) are persisted - anything else is dropped at ingest. Listings expire 7 days after `created_at` OR after 3 hours with no re-scrape; `hide_expired=true` (default on reads) filters those out. `item_summary` computes an exact median via `percentile_cont`. `/insert` is **master-only**.
- `GET /v1/market/listings[?name=&price_min=&price_max=&last_seen_after=&hide_expired=true&sort=-last_seen&limit=100&offset=0]` → `{ items: [Listing], count, total }`, Listing = `{ id, name, type, stack, price, price_each, last_seen, created_at, expires_at, expired }`. Default sort newest-`last_seen` first; pass `+price_each` to sort cheapest-first. `id` is the game's UUID v1 stringified. **Archive rate limit**: passing `hide_expired=false` (asking for expired/historical listings) pays a SECOND, tighter per-token bucket (default 10 req/min) on top of the standard cap - surfaced via `X-RateLimit-Archive-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` response headers. The default `hide_expired=true` pays only the standard cap. (Market doesn't need a "90-day" threshold like leaderboards; the in-game 7-day listing lifetime already defines fresh-vs-historical, so the archive limit fires on the opt-in flag instead of an anchor age.)
- `GET /v1/market/items` → `{ items: [<name>], count }` - item names with at least one stored listing (sorted). (The `/market` **site page** additionally decorates each item with a thumbnail: it reverses the listing's display name back to a codex entry to recover its `blueprint`, then renders it via `/v1/codexes/render`. When a name sits on several prefab roles (e.g. a piñata's item token vs its mount body) the tradable item's icon wins; a name with no codex entry, or whose top role still disagrees on the blueprint, shows no thumbnail - a wrong image is worse than none. Site-only, via the `/site/market/item-images` proxy; there is no v1 item→image endpoint.)
- For the bot's scan allow-list see `GET /v1/misc/interest-items` (moved out of market - it's tokenless so dashboards / wikis can fetch it without a key). Admin-managed via `/admin/market/interest-items` (master panel). The `/market` sidebar's collapsible item groups come from the admin-defined categories (`/admin/market/categories`, master panel; Mongo `market_item_categories`); membership is by item name so allow-list churn (deletes, bulk replace) never uncategorizes.
- `GET /v1/market/items/{name}/summary` → `{ name, count, total_price, total_stack, min_each, max_each, avg_each, median_each }` - aggregate stats across active (non-expired) listings of one item. 404 when no active listings exist.
- `POST /v1/market/insert[?timestamp=<unix>]` (multipart `file`) - **master only**. Submit the raw cfg text. Returns `{ parsed, imported, ignored_not_in_list, last_seen }`. `timestamp` overrides the `last_seen` anchor (only for back-fills). Listings are upserted by UUID - same listing re-scraped bumps `last_seen`, never duplicates. **Ingest cooldown**: same per-token, per-endpoint cap as `/v1/leaderboards/insert` (default 1 per 300s; API-token only; session-JWT replay through the portal bypasses).
- `POST /v1/market/reset` - **master only. Destructive.** TRUNCATEs the whole `market_listing` table (active + historical) and returns `{ reset: true, removed: <prior row count> }`. The interest-items allow-list is kept. Use it to clear seed/demo data before the live hourly scrape takes over. Also surfaced as a danger-zone button in the dev-portal ingest panel.
- **Listing fee and sale tax are not part of the API** - no endpoint returns them and no field carries them. They are a published *game* constant, computed client-side on the `/market` page (`site/static/market-fees.js`, exported as `window.BTTMarketFee`) for the Fees tab and for the **Fee** / **Seller nets** columns on each listing row. The fee is a cubic Bézier over control points `(50, 1500, 6000, 65000)` in `t = (min(price, 40_000_000) - 1) / (40_000_000 - 1)`, **truncated**: `fee(t) = 50(1-t)³ + 3·1500·t(1-t)² + 3·6000·t²(1-t) + 65000·t³`. Samples: 15k→51, 250k→77, 1M→165, 10M→2513, 25M→18904, 40M and above→65000 (flat). **40M is where the curve reaches its 65,000 cap, not the maximum listable price.** The fee is charged per *listing* (on its total price, not per item in the stack) at posting time; a sale refunds it and takes a 10% tax (seller nets `price × 0.90`), while an expired listing keeps no tax but loses the fee.

### Store (`store:read`) - the in-game Kiwi Store catalog

Ingested from a scraper tmod (StoreLog) that replaces `ui/kiwistore.swf`: it records everything the game engine pushes into the store window (tabs, product tiles, prices, sale stickers, limited-time-deal countdowns, class tiles, texture layers, lootbox probability text), walks every tab, and dumps it into its mod cfg; the bot POSTs that cfg to `/v1/store/insert`. Products are upserted by their **engine product code** (stable key); a price-history point is appended only when the price signature actually changes, so sales and price bumps are queryable over time. Each ingest also records **availability intervals** (present-in-store runs) so an accurate day-by-day timeline is queryable, and a product missing from the latest scrape is never deleted - it just goes `active:false` (delisted) and keeps its history. A same-origin website view of all this lives at **`/store`** (Trove Store History: a pack gallery with in-game art + a global availability timeline; in-game `.dds` textures are served from the updates CAS and decoded client-side). Prices are in-game currencies (`TWC` credits / `TWP` cubits, with patron `monthly` pricing and `sale` sticker keys); real-money SKUs carry a pre-formatted `price_string` instead. Names/labels are the game's raw localization keys (e.g. `$Store_...`) exactly as the engine sent them. `/insert` and `/reset` are **master-only**.
- `GET /v1/store/products[?category=&kind=&currency=&q=&active=true&on_sale=false&limit=100&offset=0]` → `{ items: [Product], count, total, anchor }`. Product = `{ code, kind, name, image, info, informational, tradable, prices: [{currency, cost, can_purchase, monthly, sale}], price_string, price_string_currency, price_string_sale, promo, deal_expires_at, interact_label, interact_enabled, trial_limits, class_level, class_power_rank, class_sub_name, class_icon, textures, loot_title, loot_body, categories, first_seen, last_seen, active }`. `kind` ∈ `product|starter|patron|interactable|trial|class`; `active=false` includes delisted products; `on_sale=true` filters to products currently carrying a sale sticker; `anchor` is the latest ingest's unix-seconds timestamp.
- `GET /v1/store/categories` → `{ items: [{index, label, icon, codes, count, active}], count, anchor }` - the store's tab list with display-ordered product codes.
- `GET /v1/store/timeline[?kind=&limit=1000]` → `{ anchor, span:{start,end}, items: [{code, name, kind, image, availability, first_seen, last_seen, active}], count }` - **availability bands for every product in one call**. `availability` is `[[start,end], ...]` unix-second intervals - one per continuous run the product was in-store, so a pack that left and returned shows multiple bands (honest "when was this available", which `first_seen`/`last_seen` alone can't express). Ordered most-recently-present first; `span` gives the axis bounds. Drives the store-history timeline view.
- `GET /v1/store/products/{code}` → Product + `price_history: [{ts, prices, price_string}]` + `availability: [[start,end], ...]` + `records` - one price point per ingest where the price signature changed (sales starting/ending, price bumps, purchase-option swaps); `records` = `{times_available, returns, total_days_seen, longest_run_days, first_seen, last_seen, currently_active, gap_days, price_low:{cur:n}, price_high:{cur:n}, price_changes}` (derived at-a-glance stats). 404 for an unknown code.
- `POST /v1/store/insert[?timestamp=<unix>]` (multipart `file`) - **master only**. Submit the raw StoreLog.cfg text. Returns `{ products, categories, created, price_changes, anchor, done_marker }`. Idempotent per product; `timestamp` overrides the anchor (back-fills only). Publishes a `store` SSE event on success.
- `POST /v1/store/reset` - **master only. Destructive.** Wipes every stored product/category + the ingest state (bad-ingest escape hatch); returns `{ reset: true, removed }`.

### OCR (`ocr:read`) - read character stats from a screenshot (self-hosted)

Self-hosted OCR (RapidOCR / ONNX - **no external service, no LLM**) that reads the in-game character stat sheet from a screenshot. The UI is moddable (themes, fonts, columns, language), so this doesn't trust raw OCR text: every recognized label is fuzzy-matched against a CLOSED multilingual vocabulary (English + French) so a garbled or translated label still resolves to the right stat, and every value is sanity-checked against the stat's expected type (integer vs percent) + plausible range. **Token required** (not tokenless): the OCR model is CPU-heavy, so it's gated behind `ocr:read` rather than the per-IP anon budget. The image is processed in memory and never stored.
- `POST /v1/ocr/character` (multipart `file`; PNG / JPEG / WebP / GIF / BMP, ≤12 MB) → `{ stats: { <key>: { value, unit, raw, confidence, in_range, type_match, derived } }, matched, total_known, lines }`. `stats` is keyed by canonical stat key (`physical_damage`, `magic_damage`, `maximum_health`, `critical_hit`, `critical_damage`, `power_rank`, …). `value` is an integer for count stats and a float for percent stats; `unit` ∈ `count`/`percent`; `raw` is the number exactly as OCR read it (empty when derived); `confidence` (0-1) folds label-match quality with the validation result; `in_range`/`type_match` flag a value that parsed but looks implausible for that stat (don't trust a stat with either `false`). `derived` is `true` when a value was COMPUTED rather than read: **`coefficient`** often isn't shown on the sheet, so it's derived as `floor(max(physical_damage, magic_damage) * (1 + critical_damage/100))` (the game's own formula) from those reads; when coefficient IS shown and agrees it's a confirmed read (`derived:false`), and a shown value that contradicts the formula is surfaced but flagged with low `confidence`. `matched` = how many known stats are present, `total_known` = vocabulary size, `lines` = the raw OCR text lines (transparency). Returns **503** (`service_unavailable`) if the OCR engine isn't installed on the server, **400** on an unreadable/empty image.

### Unlock Debug (site-only helper, no token)

Backs the **Unlock Debug** page (`trove.aallyn.net/unlock-debug`), which turns on Trove's built-in debug console. Trove ships the console behind one conditional jump; the endpoint rewrites it (`7C 39 68 E0 02 00 00` -> `90 90 68 E0 02 00 00`) and hands the executable straight back. **Nothing is stored** - the upload is never written to disk - and no account is needed. Gated by `feature_unlock_debug_enabled`, which **defaults OFF**: Trion runs anti-cheat and tampering with the client binary is grounds for a ban, so the whole surface 404s unless an operator deliberately turns it on. Own per-IP bucket (`unlock_debug_rate_limit_*`, 6 per 5 min).
- `POST /site/unlock-debug` (multipart `trove_exe`) -> the patched binary as `application/octet-stream` (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Trove.exe"`). **400** when no file is sent, the file is empty, it isn't a Windows executable (no `MZ`), or it doesn't contain the sequence - the last case covers an already-patched file and a build the game has since changed, and is rejected rather than returned untouched, because a silent no-op is indistinguishable from a successful patch once it's been downloaded. Body cap `unlock_debug_max_request_body_bytes` (160 MB). Legacy `GET /unlock_debug` 301s to the current page URL.

## Meta

- `GET /health` → `{ "status": "ok" }`
- `GET /openapi.json` → full machine-readable OpenAPI spec

---

## Example

```bash
export KIWI_TOKEN="kiwi_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"   # created in the portal

curl https://api.aallyn.net/v1/rotations/server-time \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KIWI_TOKEN"
```
